meta.description: Canonical, machine-readable requirements for BrainGain — the single source of truth and the single file handed off to the standalone VeriTrace viewer (which renders the catalog and the controlled documents). BrainGain has no in-app requirements page. Edit here, then run requirements/tools/build.mjs (rebuild catalog + coverage) and sync-tests.mjs (embed live results under testRun).

iec62304.rationale: Provisional Class B: BrainGain manages mandatory competency/training records; a software failure could lead to missed or expired safety-relevant training (indirect, non-serious harm). Confirm via ISO 14971 risk analysis.

source.label: Reordering of materials, questions and answers

actors.name: Administrator
actors.description: Owns the system. Manages users, job roles, trainings, and global settings. Sees and edits everything.

actors.name: Trainer
actors.description: Owns and manages their own trainings (material, quiz, recurrence). Sees who must take their trainings. Cannot manage users/roles/system settings.

actors.name: Member (Learner)
actors.description: A regular employee. Completes the trainings their job roles require.

actors.name: Organization / Business owner
actors.description: Wants demonstrable, auditable training compliance with low administrative effort.

outOfScope.text: A relational/SQL database or multi-server deployment.
Scheduled/automatic backups, retention pruning, off-site replication and archive encryption (backups are created, downloaded and restored on demand by an administrator).

requirements.title: Email/password authentication
requirements.text: Users shall authenticate with an email address and password; there is no public self-registration.

requirements.title: Land on relevant trainings after sign-in
requirements.text: After signing in, a user shall land on a view listing the trainings relevant to them.

requirements.title: Admin-only editing, reliably enforced
requirements.text: Trainings, Job Roles, and Users shall be editable only by an administrator. Access control must be enforced reliably, not merely hidden in the UI.

requirements.title: Three access levels
requirements.text: The system shall distinguish three access levels — Member, Trainer, and Administrator — and show each only the capabilities appropriate to their level.

requirements.title: Persistent session
requirements.text: A user's session shall persist across page reloads and expire after a reasonable period without re-login.

requirements.title: Sign in with Microsoft Entra ID
requirements.text: Users shall be able to sign in with their Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) work account as an alternative to email/password.

requirements.title: SSO optional & configurable
requirements.text: Microsoft SSO shall be optional and configurable by an administrator; when it is not configured/enabled, the application behaves exactly as a password-only app.

requirements.title: Configure SSO in-app
requirements.text: An administrator shall configure SSO (enable/disable, tenant, application, permitted email domains) from within the application (Settings), without code or environment changes.

requirements.title: Domain-restricted provisioning & linking
requirements.text: When a person signs in via SSO and matches an existing user (by email), their account shall be linked without changing their existing roles/permissions. If unmatched and their email domain is allowed, a new member-level account shall be created automatically; otherwise sign-in shall be refused.

requirements.title: Keep password login alongside SSO
requirements.text: Email/password login shall remain available alongside SSO.

requirements.title: Admin can view the app as another user
requirements.text: An administrator shall be able to impersonate another user — seeing the application exactly as that user does (their dashboard, due trainings, and role-appropriate navigation) — to support and troubleshoot, then return to their own session.

requirements.title: Admin manages users
requirements.text: An administrator shall create, edit, and delete users (name, email, password, access level).

requirements.title: User belongs to several roles
requirements.text: A user shall be assignable to several job roles.

requirements.title: Mark trainer/administrator
requirements.text: An administrator shall be able to mark a user as a Trainer or Administrator.

requirements.title: Bulk-import users from the clipboard
requirements.text: An administrator shall import users by pasting tabular data copied from Excel or another spreadsheet (columns Name, Email, Roles). Each row's job roles shall be matched to existing roles by name, and a row whose email matches an existing user shall update that user rather than create a duplicate.

requirements.title: Preview import changes before applying
requirements.text: Before any data is written, the administrator shall see a preview of exactly what the import will do: which users will be created, the field-level changes to existing users (name and added/removed roles), and which rows cannot be imported and why.

requirements.title: Imported users default to Member, pending activation
requirements.text: A newly imported user shall default to Member access (neither Trainer nor Administrator) with no password, and the account shall remain disabled until the user activates it.

requirements.title: Disabled accounts cannot sign in
requirements.text: A disabled account shall be unable to sign in by any method — email/password or Microsoft SSO — until it has been activated.

requirements.title: Self-set password via a one-time activation link
requirements.text: A newly imported user shall activate their account through a one-time link supplied by the administrator, choosing their own password; on success the account becomes enabled and the user is signed in. A spent or invalid link shall be refused.

requirements.title: Editable job-role list
requirements.text: An administrator shall maintain a simple, editable list of job roles (name, description).

requirements.title: Role requires trainings
requirements.text: Each job role shall require several trainings; the administrator chooses which trainings a role demands.

requirements.title: Required trainings derived from roles
requirements.text: The trainings a user must complete shall be derived from the union of their roles' required trainings (with duplicates removed).

requirements.title: Editable training list
requirements.text: The system shall maintain an editable list of trainings (name, description, category, duration).

requirements.title: Learning material (links and files)
requirements.text: Each training shall provide learning material for learners to study: web links to documents and/or uploaded files of any type. Uploaded files are downloaded and opened in the learner's installed applications; the system does not preview them. A material is a group of per-language variants (SR-152), each carrying its own label and its own link or file.

requirements.title: Multiple-choice quiz
requirements.text: Each training shall include a multiple-choice quiz. Each question shall have at least one correct answer, and may have several — a question is answered correctly only when exactly the correct answers are selected.

requirements.title: Recurrence cycle
requirements.text: Each training shall define a recurrence cycle (how often, in years, it must be repeated).

requirements.title: Due window
requirements.text: Each training shall define a due window — how early before the due date it becomes available and how long after it remains in grace before counting as overdue.

requirements.title: Trainer owns their trainings
requirements.text: A trainer shall own and manage only their own trainings; an administrator manages all trainings and may assign a training's owner.

requirements.title: Admin reorders via drag-and-drop
requirements.text: An administrator shall be able to reorder trainings via drag-and-drop, defining an explicit display order.

requirements.title: Order respected everywhere
requirements.text: The administrator-defined training order shall be respected consistently in every view that lists trainings (admin list, learner dashboard, trainee oversight, role editor).

requirements.title: Material → quiz → result flow
requirements.text: A learner shall complete a training as a flow: review material → take the quiz → see the result.

requirements.title: Server-side grading
requirements.text: The quiz shall be graded by the system, comparing the score to a configurable pass threshold; the learner must not be able to influence their own score, and correct answers must not be exposed to someone taking the test.

requirements.title: Unlimited retries; record only passes
requirements.text: A learner shall be able to retry the quiz as often as needed; only a passing attempt is recorded. Failed attempts leave the training in its current due state.

requirements.title: Computed due status
requirements.text: The system shall compute each training's due status per user (never taken, up-to-date, due now, overdue) from the last passing attempt and the training's cycle/window.

requirements.title: Dashboard of required trainings
requirements.text: The dashboard shall show the trainings required of the signed-in user, each with its current due status and a clear call to start.

requirements.title: Friendly empty state
requirements.text: The dashboard shall present a friendly empty state when no trainings are assigned.

requirements.title: Who must take each training
requirements.text: A trainer/administrator shall see, grouped by training, who is required to take it and each person's due status.

requirements.title: Filter due & email reminders
requirements.text: They shall be able to filter to only those who are due/overdue and email the relevant trainees a reminder. (Originally copy-to-clipboard; superseded by direct sending per SR-097.)

requirements.title: Global pass threshold
requirements.text: An administrator shall set a single global pass threshold that applies to all trainings at once.

requirements.title: Manage SSO from Settings
requirements.text: An administrator shall manage SSO configuration from the same Settings area (see SR-008).

requirements.title: Polished, professional UI + icon
requirements.text: The application shall present a polished, professional, modern interface with a distinctive app icon/logo.
requirements.sourceNote: fantastic user interface; very good icon

requirements.title: Petrol/teal corporate palette
requirements.text: The visual design shall follow the corporate UNICHECK design language: a dark petrol/teal palette with a black app bar and white content cards on a light neutral background (not purple). (Supersedes the original pastel-blue brief.)
requirements.sourceNote: restyled to the UNICHECK design language (stakeholder request 2026-06-11)

requirements.title: Clean corporate typography
requirements.text: Typography shall be clean and professional, using a single corporate sans-serif family in line with the UNICHECK design language. (Supersedes the earlier technical/engineered font pairing.)
requirements.sourceNote: restyled to the UNICHECK design language (stakeholder request 2026-06-11)

requirements.title: Responsive & accessible
requirements.text: The interface shall be responsive (usable on mobile and desktop) and accessible (keyboard navigable, clear focus, sensible labels).

requirements.title: Clear operation feedback
requirements.text: Data operations shall give clear feedback: loading indicators while fetching and success/error notifications on actions.

requirements.title: Searchable, collapsible lists
requirements.text: Every list in the application shall offer a text search field that filters entries by their visible content. Lists whose entries are individually expandable shall start with every entry collapsed and behave as an accordion — opening an entry closes the previously open one; there is no expand/collapse-all control. Where a list offers a "show only due" filter, the user's choice shall be remembered in their profile and applied on their next visit, from any browser. Lists whose entries open a dialog or a separate page (a training session from the dashboard) shall keep the entry that was opened last visibly marked when the list shows again, so the user sees where they were when they come back.

requirements.title: Sorted, findable lists
requirements.text: Every list, table and dropdown of entities shall be presented in a sensible, stable order (by default alphabetical by display name) so a user can find an entry quickly. Data with a deliberate order — the admin-reordered training list, enumerations (priority, status, years), and the user-import preview — keeps that order.

requirements.title: TypeScript everywhere
requirements.text: The application shall be written in TypeScript for both frontend and backend.

requirements.title: JSON-file persistence
requirements.text: Data shall be persisted to local JSON files (no external database).

requirements.title: Vue frontend
requirements.text: The frontend shall be built with Vue (not React).

requirements.title: All entities editable via UI
requirements.text: All managed entities (users, roles, trainings, settings) shall be editable through the user interface.

requirements.title: Server-side security enforcement
requirements.text: Security-sensitive operations (login result/grading/ownership/access checks, SSO token validation) shall be enforced on the server, never trusted from the client.

requirements.title: No secrets to clients
requirements.text: Secrets shall not be exposed to clients; SSO must operate without storing a client secret, so that its configuration can safely be admin-editable.

requirements.title: Easy to run; seed demo data
requirements.text: The system shall be easy to run for evaluation, seeding demo data (an admin, a trainer, a member) on first start.

requirements.title: HTTPS-only delivery
requirements.text: The application shall be delivered only over HTTPS (TLS). Plain HTTP shall not serve the app or API; HTTP requests are redirected to HTTPS.

requirements.title: Admin-managed TLS certificate
requirements.text: An administrator shall upload and replace the TLS certificate (and private key) from the Settings page, applied without downtime; the private key is never exposed to clients.

requirements.title: Monorepo backend + frontend
requirements.text: The product shall be a monorepo with a backend/ (Express + TypeScript) and a frontend/ (Vue 3 + TypeScript, Vite).

requirements.title: Run via tsx; UUID ids
requirements.text: The backend shall run via tsx (tsx watch in dev, tsx in prod) with no build step required; IDs shall be generated with crypto.randomUUID().

requirements.title: Vue 3 + Pinia + Router + axios
requirements.text: The frontend shall use Vue 3 Composition API, Pinia for state, Vue Router 4, and axios (baseURL /api); Vite shall proxy /api to the backend.

requirements.title: Tailwind + lucide + fonts
requirements.text: Styling shall use Tailwind CSS v3, icons lucide-vue-next, and Google Font Open Sans; no external UI component library.

requirements.title: JSON-file persistence
requirements.text: Persistence shall be JSON files via fs/promises; there shall be no external database.

requirements.title: First-run seed
requirements.text: On first run only (when no users exist), the backend shall seed an admin, a trainer, a member, a job role, two trainings, and the settings file.

requirements.title: Strict TypeScript, no any
requirements.text: The codebase shall use strict TypeScript with no any types (use unknown + guards).

requirements.title: CycloneDX SBOM generated by the build
requirements.text: Each package build (backend and frontend `npm run build`) shall generate a CycloneDX 1.x JSON SBOM via @cyclonedx/cyclonedx-npm into sbom/backend.cdx.json and sbom/frontend.cdx.json as its last step, listing production (runtime) dependencies only (--omit dev) with reproducible output; a root `npm run sbom` regenerates both without a full build.

requirements.title: Generic JSON stores
requirements.text: The store shall keep users/roles/trainings/sessions as JSON arrays and settings as a single object; generic helpers auto-initialize missing files and serialize with 2-space indentation.

requirements.title: User entity
requirements.text: User = { id, email, passwordHash?, name, roleIds[], isAdmin, isTrainer, entraOid?, createdAt }. passwordHash optional (SSO-only users); entraOid is the linked Entra object id.

requirements.title: JobRole entity
requirements.text: JobRole = { id, name, description, trainingIds[] }.

requirements.title: Training entity
requirements.text: Training = { id, name, description, durationMinutes (minutes; legacy hour-based records are converted ×60 by the boot/restore migration), category, ownerId, cycleYears (1-5), windowBeforeMonths (0-3), windowAfterMonths (0-3), order, materials[], questions[] (the PUBLISHED content), version, updates[], draft?, createdAt }. name, description and category are per-language maps (locale → string, en/de — see SYS-DATA-13), legacy plain strings migrating to the English entry at boot. A material is { id, variants[] } with one variant per language: { locale, label, url? | file? }; a file descriptor is { id, name, size, type } and the bytes live on disk under DATA_DIR/materials.

requirements.title: Question; answer key stripped
requirements.text: Question = { id, text, options[], correctIndices[], type }, where text and every option are per-language maps (locale → string, SYS-DATA-12) and correctIndices holds the index of every correct option and is never empty. The answer key shall never be sent to a non-owner: a PublicTraining shape strips correctIndices entirely, so a learner learns neither which options are correct nor how many.

requirements.title: Settings entity
requirements.text: Settings = { passThreshold (0-1, default 0.8), entra: { enabled, tenantId, clientId, allowedDomains[] } }; reading backfills defaults onto older files via a shallow merge.

verifiedBy.note: entra defaults backfilled; passThreshold preserved

requirements.title: SafeUser strips secrets
requirements.text: The client-facing SafeUser shall be Omit<User, 'passwordHash' | 'entraOid'>; a shared toSafeUser() shall strip both before any user is returned.

requirements.title: TrainingSession; passes only
requirements.text: TrainingSession = { id, userId, trainingId, completedAt, scorePct }; only passing attempts shall be persisted.

requirements.title: User activation fields
requirements.text: User shall gain optional isDisabled and activationToken. isDisabled gates sign-in; activationToken is the one-time activation secret. Like passwordHash, activationToken is a secret: SafeUser = Omit<User,'passwordHash'|'entraOid'|'activationToken'> and toSafeUser() strips it before any user is returned.

verifiedBy.note: GET /api/users never leaks activationToken

requirements.title: POST /login
requirements.text: POST /api/auth/login { email, password } shall match email case-insensitively, verify with bcrypt.compare, and on success return { token, user: SafeUser }; 400 on missing fields, 401 on bad credentials.

verifiedBy.note: admin login returns token + user

requirements.title: bcrypt rounds 10
requirements.text: Passwords shall be hashed with bcryptjs, salt rounds 10.

requirements.title: JWT 7d
requirements.text: The session token shall be a JWT signed with JWT_SECRET, payload { id, email, isAdmin, isTrainer }, expiry 7d.

requirements.title: GET /me rehydrate
requirements.text: GET /api/auth/me (authenticated) shall return the current SafeUser, used to rehydrate the user after a page refresh.

requirements.title: Token storage + interceptors
requirements.text: The frontend shall store the token in localStorage; axios shall attach Authorization: Bearer <token> to every request; on a 401 it shall clear the token and redirect to /login.

requirements.title: No registration endpoint
requirements.text: There shall be no public registration endpoint.

requirements.title: SSO-only cannot password-login
requirements.text: A user without a passwordHash (SSO-only) shall be unable to log in with a password (login returns 401).

verifiedBy.note: bad/no-password credentials → 401

requirements.title: Disabled accounts refused at sign-in
requirements.text: A user with isDisabled = true shall be refused by both POST /api/auth/login (generic 401, no user enumeration) and POST /api/auth/sso/entra (403), so an imported-but-not-activated account cannot sign in by any method.

verifiedBy.note: disabled account → 401 on password login

requirements.title: Account activation endpoints
requirements.text: GET /api/auth/activate/:token (public) shall return { email, name } for a still-pending account or 404. POST /api/auth/activate { token, password } (public) shall require a password of at least 8 chars, set the passwordHash, clear isDisabled, consume the one-time activationToken, and return { token, user: SafeUser } (auto sign-in). A spent/invalid token shall return 400.

verifiedBy.note: activate sets password + enables; spent token → 400

requirements.title: Self-service profile (language & UI prefs)
requirements.text: PUT /api/auth/me { locale?, prefs? } (authenticated) shall be the only self-service profile write: `locale` persists the user's language — UI languages (en, de) only, 400 otherwise — and `prefs` persists whitelisted boolean UI flags (dashboardOnlyDue, myTeamOnlyDue, traineesOnlyDue), merged per key so a view updates only its own flag; unknown keys or non-boolean values are 400, as is a body with neither field. The route returns the fresh identity payload, which every sign-in (login, SSO, activation, /me) then carries so the client applies it. It shall be refused with 403 during impersonation, because the token carries the target user's identity; the client likewise never persists a locale or preference while impersonating.

verifiedBy.note: locale round-trips through /me and login; non-UI locale 400; impersonation 403

requirements.title: MSAL popup → ID token
requirements.text: The browser shall obtain an Entra ID token using MSAL.js (@azure/msal-browser) popup flow with scopes openid profile email.

requirements.title: Public /sso/config
requirements.text: GET /api/auth/sso/config (public) shall return { enabled: false }, or { enabled: true, clientId, authority } when configured; the login page shows the Microsoft button only when enabled.

verifiedBy.note: returns enabled flag + clientId/authority

requirements.title: POST /sso/entra guards
requirements.text: POST /api/auth/sso/entra { idToken } shall return 503 when SSO is disabled/unconfigured, 400 when idToken is absent.

verifiedBy.note: 503 when disabled; 400 without idToken

requirements.title: ID-token validation
requirements.text: The backend shall validate the ID token server-side with jwks-rsa + jsonwebtoken: enforce RS256, aud = client id, iss = https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/v2.0, tid = tenant, expiry with 300s clock tolerance; JWKS cached per tenant. Invalid tokens → 401.

verifiedBy.note: self-signed-key checks: RS256/aud/iss/tid/exp/alg enforced

requirements.title: Claim extraction
requirements.text: From the validated token the system shall read oid, email (email then preferred_username), and name; a token missing oid or any email shall be rejected.

verifiedBy.note: missing oid/email rejected; preferred_username fallback

requirements.title: Link / provision resolution
requirements.text: User resolution: (1) match by entraOid; else (2) match by email and link entraOid without changing roles/admin/trainer flags — 409 if the email is already linked to a different entraOid; else (3) if the email domain is in allowedDomains, auto-create a member; else (4) 403.

verifiedBy.note: link/provision/409/403 branches reviewed

requirements.title: Issue same app JWT
requirements.text: On success the endpoint shall issue the same app JWT (signToken) and return { token, user: SafeUser }, identical to password login, so all downstream session handling is unchanged.

requirements.title: No client secret; graceful off
requirements.text: SSO shall require no client secret; its configuration shall be admin-editable and, when absent/disabled, the app shall behave exactly as a password-only app.

verifiedBy.note: no-config path leaves app password-only

requirements.title: SPA registration assumptions
requirements.text: Operation shall assume an Azure Single-Page Application registration, single-tenant, with the redirect URI set to the app origin and delegated permissions openid/profile/email.

requirements.title: Auth middleware set
requirements.text: The backend shall provide middleware: authenticate (401), requireAdmin (403), requireTrainerOrAdmin (403), requireAdminOrOwner (403 unless admin or the training's owner).

requirements.title: Admin-only mutations
requirements.text: All mutating endpoints on /api/roles and /api/users, and PUT /api/settings, shall require admin.

requirements.title: Training mutation guards
requirements.text: POST /api/trainings shall require trainer-or-admin; PUT/DELETE /api/trainings/:id shall require admin-or-owner; only admins may set/change ownerId; PUT /api/trainings/reorder shall require admin.

requirements.title: Router guard
requirements.text: The frontend router shall enforce route meta requiresAuth/requiresAdmin/requiresTrainerOrAdmin, redirecting unauthenticated users to /login and unauthorized users to /dashboard; after a refresh it shall fetchMe() before role checks.

requirements.title: Role-gated sidebar
requirements.text: The sidebar shall render only the navigation items appropriate to the user's level (defense-in-depth, not the sole control).

requirements.title: Permission matrix
requirements.text: The system shall conform to the documented API permission matrix for every role/endpoint pair.

requirements.title: Impersonation token issuance
requirements.text: POST /api/auth/impersonate/:userId (admin only) shall issue a JWT scoped to the target user — carrying the target's id, email, isAdmin and isTrainer so every endpoint and guard renders as that user — and additionally carrying the impersonator's id and email for audit and the nesting guard.

verifiedBy.note: impersonation token decodes to the target identity plus impersonatorId/email of the admin

requirements.title: Impersonation guards
requirements.text: The impersonation endpoint shall require an administrator (403 otherwise), refuse impersonating oneself (400), refuse nesting when the caller's token already carries an impersonatorId (409), and return 404 for an unknown target user.

verifiedBy.note: self → 400, nesting → 409, non-admin → 403, unknown → 404, no token → 401

requirements.title: Client view-as session
requirements.text: The frontend shall start impersonation from the Users page (the View-as action), park the admin token and activate the impersonation token so the whole app renders as the target user, show a persistent banner naming the impersonated user with a Stop control, and on Stop restore the parked admin token and reload the admin profile; a fresh sign-in clears any parked token.

verifiedBy.note: View as → banner + member-only nav; Stop restores the admin session (Edge via Playwright)

requirements.title: /api/users CRUD
requirements.text: /api/users shall provide admin-only CRUD: create { name, email, password, roleIds, isAdmin, isTrainer }; update with optional password (blank keeps the current one).

requirements.title: Users page
requirements.text: The Users page shall list users in a table and edit them in a wide centered modal dialog titled with the user's name, with a role multi-select and isAdmin/isTrainer toggles.

requirements.title: POST /api/users/import
requirements.text: POST /api/users/import (admin-only) { rows:[{name,email,roles}], commit } shall compute a per-row plan — create | update | unchanged | error — matching emails to existing users and role names to roles (both case-insensitive), with field diffs (name; roles added/removed) for updates. A row is an error (never applied) when name/email is missing or invalid, the email duplicates an earlier row, or any role name is unknown. With commit=false it writes nothing (preview); with commit=true it creates each new user as a disabled Member with no password and a one-time activationToken (returned for that row), and fully replaces name + roleIds on matched existing users. GET /api/users/:id/activation re-fetches a pending user's token. The Import Users page tokenizes the paste, renders the plan (badges, diffs, errors), and lists the activation links after commit.

verifiedBy.note: dry-run plan + commit create/update; unknown role & duplicate → error

requirements.title: /api/roles CRUD
requirements.text: /api/roles shall provide admin-only CRUD.

requirements.title: Role editor training multiselect
requirements.text: The Role editor shall present a multi-select checkbox list of all trainings, writing the selection to trainingIds.

requirements.title: Role editor honours order
requirements.text: The Role editor's training list shall follow the admin-defined training order.

requirements.title: GET / ordered
requirements.text: GET /api/trainings shall return trainings sorted by order ascending; admins see all, trainers may pass ?mine=1; the answer key (correctIndices) is stripped for non-owners.

verifiedBy.note: order respected; answer key stripped

requirements.title: GET /:id
requirements.text: GET /api/trainings/:id shall return one training; for non-owners the answer key AND the work-in-progress draft are stripped — the session quiz always runs on the published content.

requirements.title: POST / append order
requirements.text: POST /api/trainings shall set a trainer's own ownerId (admins may target any owner) and append the new training to the end of the order (order = max + 1).

requirements.title: PUT /:id preserves order
requirements.text: PUT /api/trainings/:id shall update an owned/any training (admin-or-owner) without changing order; only admins may change ownerId. Metadata applies immediately; materials/questions are STAGED as the draft (SYS-UPD-07) — the published content is never written by PUT.

requirements.title: DELETE /:id
requirements.text: DELETE /api/trainings/:id shall be permitted only to admin-or-owner.

requirements.title: PUT /reorder
requirements.text: PUT /api/trainings/reorder { ids[] } (admin-only) shall set each training's order to its position in the array; it shall be registered before the /:id route.

verifiedBy.note: reorder persists; admin-only (trainer 403)

requirements.title: Order is single source
requirements.text: The list endpoints (/, /mine, /trainees) shall sort by order; legacy records missing order shall be backfilled by file position and persisted, making order the single source of truth.

verifiedBy.note: order respected across /, /mine, /trainees

requirements.title: Drag-and-drop reorder UI
requirements.text: The Trainings page shall let admins reorder via drag-and-drop (grip handle); a normal row click still opens the editor; trainers shall not see the handle; dropping persists the new order via the reorder endpoint.

requirements.title: Training editor fields
requirements.text: The training editor shall manage the localized name/category/description (one input per content language — see SYS-TRN-17), cycleYears (1-5), windowBeforeMonths/windowAfterMonths (0-3), localized materials (per configured language: label plus a web link or an uploaded file of any type — no preview; see SYS-TRN-15), questions (text/options/correctIndices — several options may be marked correct), and — admin only — ownerId.

requirements.title: Content-readiness flags & action gating
requirements.text: A training needs material to study (at least one material — every stored material carries a link or an uploaded file in some language, SR-041) and questions to be tested on (SR-042) before trainees can use it. The Trainings list shall flag only what needs attention (no material / no test, collapsed into one combined flag when both are missing) so trainers see what to finish — a complete training carries no readiness marker, and the start/test actions shall be disabled until the required content exists: Start needs both material and questions; the quiz step needs questions.

implementedBy.symbol: Start test disabled when no questions

requirements.title: Material file upload & download
requirements.text: POST /api/trainings/materials (trainer/admin) shall accept a single uploaded file of any type — the raw bytes as the request body, original name/type as query params — store it under DATA_DIR/materials, and return a { id, name, size, type } descriptor that the client binds to a material variant (the blob itself is language-agnostic). GET /api/trainings/materials/:fileId shall stream a stored file to any authenticated user as an attachment download (no preview); the fileId shall be validated as a UUID to prevent path traversal. Bytes are deleted exactly when nothing references them anymore: replacing a draft file on save deletes the replaced draft upload, publishing deletes published uploads the promotion superseded, discarding a draft deletes its draft-only uploads, and deleting a training deletes the union of its published and draft uploads.

verifiedBy.note: upload returns descriptor; download streams the bytes; bad/forged ids rejected

requirements.title: computeDue()
requirements.text: A single computeDue() shall derive status from the last passing session: dueDate = lastPassed + cycleYears, windowOpen = dueDate − windowBeforeMonths, windowClose = dueDate + windowAfterMonths, yielding never/up-to-date/due/overdue; reused by both /mine and /trainees.

requirements.title: GET /mine
requirements.text: GET /api/trainings/mine shall return DueTraining[] for the current user's required trainings (union of role trainingIds, deduped), in order, with server-computed status.

requirements.title: Session flow
requirements.text: The Session page (/session/:trainingId) shall implement the flow material → quiz → result. The material step shall list the training's materials resolved to the learner's chosen language (SYS-SES-08) — link variants open in a new tab, file variants download to open in installed apps.

requirements.title: POST /grade server-side
requirements.text: POST /api/sessions/grade { trainingId, answers[], reauth } shall grade server-side against the stored answer key, compare scorePct to Settings.passThreshold, persist a TrainingSession only if passed, and return { scorePct, passed, passThreshold }. answers[i] is the set of option indices the learner selected for question i. Grading runs only after the completion signature in `reauth` is verified (SYS-SES-12).

requirements.title: Unlimited retries
requirements.text: A learner shall be able to submit /grade repeatedly; failed attempts shall not be recorded and shall leave the due state unchanged.

requirements.title: GET /sessions/mine
requirements.text: GET /api/sessions/mine shall return the current user's passing sessions.

requirements.title: GET /settings
requirements.text: GET /api/settings (any authenticated user) shall return the full Settings.

verifiedBy.note: returns passThreshold + entra

requirements.title: PUT /settings merge
requirements.text: PUT /api/settings (admin) shall be a partial merge: validate/clamp passThreshold to 0.5–1 when present, and when entra is present coerce booleans, trim ids, and accept allowedDomains as an array or comma-separated string — so SSO and threshold save independently.

verifiedBy.note: merge independence; domain sanitization

requirements.title: Settings page cards
requirements.text: The Settings page shall present a pass-threshold card, an Entra ID SSO card (enable toggle; tenant id; client id; allowed domains; a hint showing the SPA redirect URI) and an automatic-backup card (enable toggle; interval in days; number of automatic backups to keep), each with its own save/list action.

verifiedBy.note: settings round-trip persists

requirements.title: Reveal-wrong-questions setting
requirements.text: Settings shall carry revealWrongQuestions: boolean, defaulting to false (readSettings backfills records saved before the field existed). PUT /api/settings shall coerce it to a boolean when present and leave it untouched otherwise; the pass-threshold card on the Settings page shall offer the toggle with a hint that the correct answers are never shown, saved by the card's save action.

verifiedBy.note: defaults to false; PUT round-trips the toggle

requirements.title: Dashboard cards
requirements.text: The Dashboard shall load /api/trainings/mine and render a responsive card grid; each card shows a due-status corner tag, name, category, description, a recurrence-and-duration line (duration formatted as hours and minutes), and a Start action. The header subtitle shall report the assigned and due counts plus the summed duration of the due trainings; an empty state shall be shown when nothing is assigned.

requirements.title: Due-only dashboard filter
requirements.text: The dashboard shall render an "only show due trainings" checkbox next to the list controls, checked by default, that hides trainings whose due status is up-to-date; never/due/overdue trainings always show. The filter combines with the search box, and unchecking it reveals the up-to-date trainings. The checked state is persisted to the user's profile (prefs.dashboardOnlyDue) and restored when the dashboard loads.

verifiedBy.note: checked by default; an up-to-date training appears only after unchecking

requirements.title: GET /trainees grouped
requirements.text: GET /api/trainings/trainees shall return TraineeGroup[] (admins: all trainings; trainers: owned), grouped per training in order, each trainee carrying server-computed status and dueDate.

requirements.title: Trainees page
requirements.text: The Trainees page shall show collapsible per-training groups (collapsed on entry, at most one open at a time), a 'only due/overdue' filter persisted to the profile (prefs.traineesOnlyDue), and per-group + global email actions that send a reminder to the shown trainees via POST /api/mail/send (recipients bcc'd), with a confirming toast — or a pointer to the SMTP settings while email is unconfigured.

requirements.title: Petrol palette
requirements.text: The theme shall use the defined petrol CSS-variable palette (content background #EDF1F1, sidebar #0E4A4D, accent #156A6E, petrol 50–900 scale, light desaturated teal tints, black #1A1A1A app bar) with an orange secondary accent (#FB923C: active-nav marker, page-bar tab underline, due-status); green/red otherwise appear as status colours. Native form controls and the in-page select picker follow the petrol accent.

requirements.title: Typography
requirements.text: All text shall use the Open Sans family (Segoe UI / system-ui fallback); both the sans and mono Tailwind font stacks resolve to it for a uniform corporate look.

requirements.title: Logo component
requirements.text: The BrainGainLogo component shall render the official PTW corporate logo (red triangle + PTW wordmark + 'The Dosimetry Company', vector SVG; size prop, onDark white-lettering variant for dark surfaces); the favicon is a BrainGain-specific mark (graduation-cap glyph on a petrol tile, vector SVG) instead of the PTW logo, so the app tab is distinguishable from other PTW tools.

requirements.title: App chrome + sidebar layout
requirements.text: The layout shall be a black app bar (logo, app name, user-initials menu with a flagged language switch that persists the choice to the profile, and logout) over a petrol page bar (section title, date), with a fixed 240 px dark-petrol sidebar + scrollable content below.

requirements.title: Responsive & accessible
requirements.text: The UI shall be responsive (375 px–1440 px) and accessible (keyboard navigable, visible focus rings, sensible aria-labels).

requirements.title: Loading + toasts
requirements.text: Every data fetch shall show a loading/skeleton state; every API call shall be wrapped in try/catch surfacing success/error toasts via a global toast store.

requirements.title: List search & collapse
requirements.text: Each list page shall render a shared ListControls toolbar with a search box that filters entries by a case-insensitive substring match over their visible text (showing a shown/total count and a 'no matches' state). Pages whose entries are individually expandable (My Team, Trainees) start fully collapsed and keep at most one entry open at a time — opening another closes the previous one; the toolbar renders only the search box, with no expand-all/collapse-all control. The "show only due" filters (dashboard, My Team, Trainees) are persisted to the profile via PUT /api/auth/me { prefs } and restored on the next visit. Lists whose entries open a dialog (Trainings, Users) mark the entry opened last (data-selected) and keep the marker after the dialog closes; the dashboard likewise marks the card whose session was started last (kept in sessionStorage, since starting navigates to another page).

requirements.title: Entity lists sorted by name
requirements.text: Lists, tables and dropdowns of entities are sorted alphabetically by display name at the data source: users, roles and org units (and the dropdowns/checkboxes built from them), the org-unit head/parent pickers and member picker, training owners, the My Team members, the Trainees groups and trainees, and the dashboard cards. Deliberately-ordered data keeps its order: the admin-reorderable training list, enum dropdowns (priority/status/years), and the user-import preview.

requirements.title: Language flags
requirements.text: Language flags are rendered as SVGs (flag-icons CSS classes; emoji flags do not render on Windows), accessible via role=img with the native language name: beside the user-menu language dropdown, on the editor's per-language rows, and on session material cards ONLY when the shown variant is not in the user's language — matching material carries no flag. English deliberately uses the US flag; flag codes come only from the locale catalog, never derived from language codes.

verifiedBy.note: flag elements (fi-us, fi-de) render in the settings card and language switch

requirements.title: Server-side enforcement
requirements.text: All security-sensitive logic — credential checks, quiz grading, ownership and access checks, and SSO token validation — shall be enforced on the server and never trusted from the client.

requirements.title: No secret leakage
requirements.text: The system shall never transmit passwordHash, entraOid, the quiz answer key (correctIndices), or any secret to clients, and SSO shall function without storing a client secret.

requirements.title: Single HTTPS origin serves API + SPA
requirements.text: The backend shall run an HTTPS server that serves both the /api routes and the built SPA (frontend/dist) from one origin; the SPA fallback returns index.html for non-/api GETs.

verifiedBy.note: curl -k https://localhost:3011/api/health → ok; / returns SPA

requirements.title: HTTP redirects to HTTPS
requirements.text: A minimal HTTP listener shall answer every request with a 308 redirect to the HTTPS URL; no app/API content is served over HTTP.

verifiedBy.note: curl -I http://localhost:3010/x → 308 Location https://…

requirements.title: Self-signed bootstrap on first run
requirements.text: If no certificate exists at startup, the server shall generate and persist a self-signed certificate so HTTPS starts immediately (no lockout before an admin uploads a real cert).

requirements.title: Cert/key stored privately; metadata-only exposure
requirements.text: The private key and certificate shall be stored under data/tls/ (git-ignored) and never returned by any API; only non-secret metadata (subject/issuer/validity/fingerprint/source) is surfaced via Settings.

requirements.title: Upload validates + hot-swaps the certificate
requirements.text: POST /api/settings/certificate (admin) shall validate the PEM and that the private key matches the certificate, then hot-swap the running server via setSecureContext (no restart). Invalid/mismatched input → 400.

requirements.title: Certificate endpoints are admin-only
requirements.text: GET /api/settings/certificate returns metadata only; POST /api/settings/certificate and /certificate/self-signed require admin (403 otherwise).

verifiedBy.note: non-admin → 403; GET returns metadata only

requirements.title: Settings TLS card
requirements.text: The Settings page shall show the active certificate metadata and let an admin upload cert/key/chain PEM files (read client-side and POSTed) and regenerate a self-signed certificate.

requirements.title: Dev server is HTTPS too
requirements.text: The Vite dev server shall run over HTTPS (auto self-signed via @vitejs/plugin-basic-ssl) and proxy /api to the backend over HTTPS (secure:false).

requirements.title: HSTS header
requirements.text: Responses shall include a Strict-Transport-Security header so browsers only ever use HTTPS for this origin.

requirements.title: Requirement test & coverage traceability
requirements.text: The requirements dataset shall record, for every requirement and validation test, the automated and manual tests that exercise it plus an overall coverage summary, so traceability and coverage travel with the dataset.

requirements.title: Training plan document (reviewable, DMS)
requirements.text: An administrator or unit head shall be able to generate a Training Plan as a controlled PDF: the trainings, a roles × trainings matrix (checkmarks for each role's assigned trainings) and a members × roles matrix (checkmarks for each member's assigned roles). It covers the members the generating user is responsible for (an admin: the whole organization; a head: the members in the units they head). It is previewed in-app before download for review and transfer to the document management system (DMS).

requirements.title: Send emails from the system
requirements.text: After an administrator configures an SMTP server in Settings, the system shall send emails directly (e.g. training reminders). Where the app previously only copied recipient addresses to the clipboard, it shall instead send a ready-to-go message with sensible default content; recipients are bcc'd for privacy and the SMTP password is never returned by the API.

requirements.title: Test & coverage data in the dataset
requirements.text: build.mjs shall scan the backend, e2e and manual test artifacts and write each requirement's and VT's coverage plus a meta.coverage summary into requirements.json.

verifiedBy.note: build.mjs --check fails on coverage/data drift

requirements.title: Training plan document generator
requirements.text: The Trainings page (admins and unit heads) shall build a Training Plan PDF with three sections — all trainings (name, category, duration, cycle); a roles × trainings matrix; and a members × roles matrix. Each matrix marks assignments with a green cross and labels its columns with the full training/role name rotated onto up to two lines in the header (no codes); a matrix that fits on a page is not split across pages. Each section's chapter title is the table's own first header row, so the title always sits with its table (repeating atop continuation pages). Members are scoped to who the user is responsible for: all users for an admin, or the head's unit subtree (GET /org-units/my-team) otherwise. The document carries a controlled-document header (document id, company, date, responsible-for scope) and prepared/reviewed/approved signature lines, is rendered to page images for inline review, and is downloaded only from the open preview (view-before-download).

requirements.title: SMTP settings & mail service
requirements.text: Settings stores an SMTP configuration (enabled, host, port, secure, username, password, fromName, fromAddress). The password is a secret: GET/PUT /api/settings redact it to '' and expose only smtp.passwordSet, and a blank password on save keeps the stored one. A nodemailer-based mail service sends through it; POST /api/mail/send (trainer/admin) validates recipients/subject/text and returns 503 when SMTP is not configured, and POST /api/mail/test (admin) sends a verification email to the caller.

requirements.title: Email trainees instead of copying addresses
requirements.text: The Trainees page sends reminder emails via POST /api/mail/send instead of copying addresses to the clipboard: a per-group button emails that training's due trainees and an "email everyone" button emails all shown trainees, each with a sensible default subject and body (recipients are bcc'd). A 503 response is surfaced as a hint to configure SMTP in Settings.

requirements.title: Tests & results are searchable, traceable objects
requirements.text: Automated and manual tests, their results, and the software safety classification shall be recorded as first-class, searchable objects in the requirements dataset, so verification evidence travels with the dataset (consumed by downstream viewers and reports).

requirements.title: Software safety classification recorded & cited
requirements.text: The software safety class (Class B) shall be recorded in the dataset (meta.iec62304) so the classification travels with the requirements for downstream documents.

requirements.title: Test-case catalog in the dataset
requirements.text: build.mjs shall parse the backend and e2e suites into a testCases[] catalog (id, name, kind, file, covers), preserving authored manual cases, so the catalog travels with the dataset for the downstream viewer.

requirements.title: Test results captured & surfaced
requirements.text: sync-tests.mjs shall run the suites and embed per-test pass/fail/skip plus a run date under testRun in requirements.json.

requirements.title: Single org-unit membership & hierarchy
requirements.text: Every user belongs to exactly one organizational unit. Units form a hierarchy (each unit has an optional parent unit).

requirements.title: One responsible head per unit
requirements.text: Each organizational unit has exactly one head, who is responsible for everyone in that unit and all of its sub-units.

requirements.title: Head oversight of training status
requirements.text: A unit head can review the training due/overdue status of everyone in their unit and its sub-units.

requirements.title: Org unit in user import
requirements.text: Bulk user import supports an Org Unit column, matched to an existing unit by name.

requirements.title: Editable company name
requirements.text: An admin can edit the company name in Settings; it names the top-level (root) organizational unit.

requirements.title: /api/org-units CRUD
requirements.text: /api/org-units provides admin-only create/update/delete and authenticated read of organizational units (id, name, parentId, headUserId).

requirements.title: Hierarchy integrity
requirements.text: Re-parenting that would create a cycle is rejected (400); a unit with sub-units or member users cannot be deleted (409).

requirements.title: Membership & migration
requirements.text: Users carry orgUnitId. A startup migration seeds a single root unit named from Settings.companyName and backfills every user; user create/import default a missing unit to the root.

requirements.title: Import Org Unit column
requirements.text: POST /api/users/import resolves an Org Unit value to a unit by name (case-insensitive); an unknown name flags the row as an error; a blank value defaults a new user to the root unit.

requirements.title: Head oversight endpoint
requirements.text: GET /api/org-units/my-team returns every member in the caller-headed units and their sub-units, each with their required trainings and due status; empty when the caller heads no unit.

requirements.title: Editable company name
requirements.text: PUT /api/settings accepts companyName (admin-only) and renames the root org unit to match.

requirements.title: Bulk add members to a unit
requirements.text: POST /api/org-units/:id/members (admin-only) moves several users into a unit at once; unknown user ids are ignored and the count of users actually moved is returned.

requirements.title: Head training-status report (signable, DMS)
requirements.text: For the units a head is responsible for, the head can generate a training-status report as a PDF — previewed in-app before download — to sign and store in a DMS.

requirements.title: Back up all application data
requirements.text: An administrator shall be able to create, on demand, a complete backup of all application data — users, job roles, trainings (including their quiz answer keys), training sessions, organizational units, global settings and every uploaded learning-material file. The backup shall be a single ZIP archive kept on the server so the data can be recovered after an accidental change, a bad import or a host failure.

requirements.title: See the stored backups and download one
requirements.text: An administrator shall see a list of all backups held on the server, each identified by its archive name, creation date, size and what it contains, and shall be able to download any individual backup as a ZIP file for off-server safekeeping.

requirements.title: Download all backups as one file
requirements.text: An administrator shall be able to download every stored backup in one action, delivered as a single ZIP file containing the individual archives, so a complete backup history can be transferred in one step.

requirements.title: Upload a backup archive
requirements.text: An administrator shall be able to upload a backup archive produced earlier or on another installation, so that it joins the list of stored backups and becomes available to restore. An uploaded file that is not a valid BrainGain backup shall be refused with a reason and shall not be stored.

requirements.title: Restore all data from a backup
requirements.text: An administrator shall be able to restore any listed backup, replacing all current application data with the contents of that archive. Because the action is destructive it shall require an explicit confirmation, and the system shall automatically snapshot the current data beforehand so that an unintended restore can itself be undone. A restore shall either apply completely or leave the existing data untouched.

requirements.title: Backups are administrator-only and delete-able
requirements.text: Only administrators shall be able to create, list, download, upload, restore or delete backups, because an archive contains every record in the system — including password hashes, activation tokens and the stored SMTP password — and a restore overwrites all data. Administrators shall be able to delete backups they no longer need. Backup archives shall not include the TLS private key.

requirements.title: Questions with several correct answers
requirements.text: A trainer shall be able to mark more than one answer of a quiz question as correct, so questions of the form "which of these are examples of X?" can be asked. Every question shall keep at least one correct answer, and the trainer shall see at a glance which answers are marked correct.

requirements.title: A multi-answer question is only passed when answered exactly
requirements.text: For a question with several correct answers, the learner shall have to select exactly those answers for the question to count as correct — an incomplete selection earns no partial credit and selecting every option shall not pass. The learner shall not be told how many answers are correct; the multi-select control (checkboxes, as opposed to the radio buttons of a single-choice question) is the indication that more than one may be — there is no textual prompt.

requirements.title: The training editor stays scannable as a training grows
requirements.text: The editor for a training shall remain readable however much the training contains. Its parts shall be grouped into sections that can be opened and closed individually, each stating what it holds while closed, so an author is never confronted with the whole record at once and can go straight to the part they came to change. Quiz questions in particular shall each fold down to a single line, since they are what makes a training grow.

requirements.title: Single-choice questions
requirements.text: A trainer shall be able to set a question's type to single-choice — including on an existing question — whenever it has exactly one correct answer; a question with several correct answers shall stay multiple-choice until its answer key is reduced to one. Questions saved before the type existed shall keep behaving as multiple-choice, and a newly added question shall start as single-choice.

requirements.title: Single-choice questions are answered with radio buttons
requirements.text: A learner shall answer a single-choice question with radio buttons — selecting an answer replaces the previous selection — while multiple-choice questions keep the multi-select control. Grading shall remain exact-match: a submission carrying more than one answer for a single-choice question is wrong.

requirements.title: Optionally reveal wrongly answered questions after a failed test
requirements.text: An administrator shall be able to enable an option — off by default — so that a learner who fails a test is shown which questions were answered wrong. Only the questions are named, never the correct answers, and a passed attempt shall not reveal anything even when it was imperfect.

requirements.title: Localized learning material
requirements.text: Learning material shall be localized in English and German: a material is a group of per-language variants, each with its own label and its own content (a web link or an uploaded file), and at least one variant must be filled per material. The session content follows the user's language (the UI language switch is the single place to change it); per material the matching variant is shown, falling back to English when the user's language is missing — and when English is missing too, every variant of that material is offered. Material saved before localization existed becomes the English variant of its own material.

requirements.title: Per-user profile language
requirements.text: Each user's language choice shall be persisted to their profile via a self-service endpoint and applied when they sign in, on any device. It doubles as the UI language and as the default material language in a training session. Language flags shall enrich the UI wherever languages are offered.

requirements.title: Localized quiz questions and answers
requirements.text: Quiz questions and their answer options shall be localizable: each text carries per-language versions, with at least one language filled, while the option structure and the answer key stay shared across languages. The learner's session language resolves each text with the material logic — chosen language, then English, then every filled language — marking anything not in the chosen language with the shown language's flag; grading is unaffected by the display language. Pre-localization records become English entries, and the live bilingual texts (German and English crammed into one string) are separated into proper per-language entries.

requirements.title: Dashboard shows only due trainings by default
requirements.text: The learner dashboard shall offer an "only show due trainings" filter that is selected by default, so the dashboard reads as a work list of what still has to be done. Unselecting it shall also show the up-to-date trainings (e.g. to review one that is not due yet). The choice shall be remembered in the user's profile and applied on their next visit.

requirements.title: Localized training name, category and description
requirements.text: A training's name, description and category shall be localizable in English and German: each field carries per-language versions, and a training must be nameable in at least one language (description and category may stay empty). Every display of these fields — dashboard cards, lists, dialogs, PDFs and reminder mail texts — follows the user's language, falling back to English when the user's language is missing, and to every filled language joined together when English is missing too. The live bilingual strings are separated into proper per-language entries; anything saved before localization existed becomes the English entry.

requirements.title: Automatic scheduled backups
requirements.text: The system shall create backups automatically on an administrator-defined schedule: an interval in days (at least one) between automatic backups, and a retention count (at least one) so that only the newest N automatic backups are kept — the oldest automatic backup is deleted first, while manually created, uploaded and pre-restore backups are never deleted by retention. Automatic backups shall be off by default, and a run the server missed (for example because it was switched off) shall be caught up at the next start.

requirements.title: Audit trail of administrative and security-relevant actions
requirements.text: The system shall record an audit trail entry for every administrative data change (users, roles, trainings, organizational units, settings), authentication event (successful and failed sign-in, SSO sign-in, account activation, impersonation), backup lifecycle action (create — manual and automatic —, upload, delete, restore and failed restore) and recorded training completion. Each entry shall carry a timestamp, the acting user (including the impersonating administrator when the action happened inside an impersonation session; system-initiated and unauthenticated events carry no actor), the action, the affected entity, and, for updates, the changed fields with their before/after values. Secret values (password hashes, activation tokens, the SMTP password, quiz answer keys) shall never appear in the audit trail in plaintext.

requirements.title: Administrators can inspect and export the audit trail
requirements.text: An administrator shall be able to view the audit trail in the application — newest entries first, filtered by action, affected entity type, free text and date range — and export the filtered trail as a CSV file. Non-administrators shall have no access to the audit trail.

requirements.title: Audit trail is retained indefinitely, backed up, and survives restore
requirements.text: Audit entries shall never be pruned or rewritten. Every backup archive shall carry a copy of the audit log as evidence, yet restoring a backup shall never overwrite or erase the local audit trail — the restore itself is recorded as a new entry, and an archived audit copy is never imported, including on a fresh installation.

requirements.title: Materials confirmation before the test — and as completion evidence for test-less trainings
requirements.text: When a learner starts a training test, the application shall first show a confirmation dialog in which the learner confirms being aware of all the materials provided for the training; the confirmation shall be recorded in the audit trail. A training without test questions shall still be startable (the missing test shall not disable the start action): after the learner confirms the materials, the training counts as completed — the audited confirmation together with the persisted session is the evidence that the learner did the training.

requirements.title: Trainer contact hint around the test
requirements.text: The application shall tell the trainee whom to contact with questions about a training: the owning trainer's name, organizational unit and email address — the data that identifies the trainer in the company address list. The hint shall be shown in the materials confirmation dialog before the test starts and on the result screen after the test, for passed and failed attempts alike.

requirements.title: Explicit publish step for training content updates
requirements.text: When a trainer or administrator saves a training whose materials or test changed, the application shall offer an explicit publish step — saving alone shall never notify anyone or change what trainees see, and the editor can skip the step, keeping the change as an unpublished draft. When publishing with notification, the editor shall choose what assignees must do — fully retake the training (materials and test) or only review the updated materials and confirm — and shall set the deadline (a sensible default pre-filled).

requirements.title: Update-triggered due state
requirements.text: A published training update shall put the training back into a due-like state for every assignee whose last pass predates the update — a different sort of due than the recurrence cycle, marked with its own distinct badge (with the update deadline) in the learner's due list and every oversight view, and included by the "only due" filters. Users who never completed the training are unaffected (they meet the published content on their first pass; drafts stay invisible until published). When the recurrence cycle itself is due or overdue, the cycle status takes precedence — a new passing session satisfies both. With several pending updates, the one with the earliest deadline governs.

requirements.title: Email notification on published updates
requirements.text: Publishing a training update shall notify the affected users (those who completed the training before the update) by email, with editable, sensible default content shown to the editor before sending; recipients are bcc'd for privacy and disabled accounts are skipped. When email cannot be sent (SMTP unconfigured, no recipients, or a send failure), the update shall still be published and the editor informed.

requirements.title: Completing an update: retake or recorded confirmation
requirements.text: A retake-mode update shall be cleared only by a new passing session — a normal completion that also restarts the regular training cycle. A confirm-mode update shall be cleared by the learner reviewing the updated materials and confirming; the confirmation is persisted as evidence and audited, no test is required, and the regular cycle date stays unchanged. A confirmation shall never clear a retake-mode update.

requirements.title: Withdraw a published update
requirements.text: The trainer who owns a training (or an administrator) shall be able to withdraw a published update, clearing the pending obligation for everyone. The withdrawal is audited; the training version is not rolled back.

requirements.title: Training content version
requirements.text: Every training shall carry a simple content version: 0 means never published (trainees cannot use the training and no version is shown), the first publish creates version 1, and every further publish increments it (2, 3, 4, …). The version never rolls back — withdrawing an update or discarding a draft keeps the version, so version numbers are never reused. Learner-facing views shall show no version numbers — versions are a trainer-side concept. The trainings list shall show the current version together with the date of the last update (when the current version was published) and the training editor the current version beside its title; an unpublished training shows no version and is flagged "Not published yet" instead.

requirements.title: Trainees see only published training versions
requirements.text: Trainees shall see and use ONLY a training's last published content. Editor changes to materials or the test are held as a work-in-progress draft that no learner-facing view or flow ever serves. A newly created training starts unpublished: assigned learners see it as "in preparation" — visible but not startable — and it cannot be completed by any path (including the API) until the editor publishes version 1.

requirements.title: Silent publish
requirements.text: When publishing, the editor shall choose how the change goes live: "publish and notify" (the update obligation with mode, deadline and email, as before) or "publish silently" — the draft becomes the next version without notifying anyone and without creating any obligation (for minor fixes and for the first version, which is always published silently since nobody could have completed it). Skipping the publish step keeps the change as a draft.

requirements.title: Discard a draft
requirements.text: The trainer who owns a training (or an administrator) shall be able to discard its draft, reverting the work-in-progress to the published state. The discard is audited; the published content and version are untouched.

requirements.title: Identity re-confirmation at completion
requirements.text: When completing a training test — with or without questions — the learner shall re-confirm their identity at that moment by entering their credentials again: the password of the signed-in account, or a fresh Microsoft sign-in for SSO-linked accounts without a local password. The confirmation shall be verified against the ACTING account (an impersonating administrator cannot complete a training for someone else), a rejected confirmation shall not grade or record anything, and the confirmation method — as well as every rejected attempt — shall be stored in the audit log.

requirements.title: Reordering of materials, questions and answers
requirements.text: The training editor shall let the author reorder learning materials, test questions and the answer options within a question. The arranged order is the order learners see (materials list, quiz question sequence, option sequence), the answer key shall keep marking the same answers when options move, and — like every content edit — a new order becomes visible to learners only when published.

requirements.title: Software bill of materials (SBOM)
requirements.text: For cybersecurity transparency, the application build shall generate a software bill of materials (SBOM) in the CycloneDX format (JSON, the industry standard) covering the runtime dependencies of both the backend and the frontend, so the shipped third-party components are known and can be screened for vulnerabilities.

requirements.title: Training status report PDF
requirements.text: The My Team page builds a Training Status Report PDF from the head's subtree (member × required training with due status) carrying a header, summary and prepared/reviewed/approved signature fields (as every DMS document does); it is rendered to page images for inline review and downloaded only from the open preview (view-before-download).

requirements.title: POST /api/backups creates an archive
requirements.text: POST /api/backups (admin) shall build a ZIP of the current data directory and store it as data/backups/<uuid>.zip with a sibling <uuid>.meta.json descriptor { id, fileName, createdAt, size, source, contents }, returning 201 and that descriptor. The archive shall carry a manifest.json identifying the producing app and format version, the JSON stores under data/, and every material file under data/materials/. From format version 2 the manifest also records the data version (dataVersion) and the producing app version (appVersion), and the archive carries data/_meta.json as a read-only passenger.

verifiedBy.note: create → 201 + descriptor; the .zip and sidecar exist on disk

requirements.title: List and delete backups
requirements.text: GET /api/backups (admin) shall return the stored backup descriptors newest first. DELETE /api/backups/:id (admin) shall remove the archive and its descriptor and return { deleted: true }; deleting an unknown id shall be 404.

requirements.title: GET /api/backups/:id/download streams one archive
requirements.text: GET /api/backups/:id/download (admin) shall return the archive bytes as application/zip with a Content-Disposition attachment naming the descriptor's fileName (ASCII form plus filename*=UTF-8''). The :id path segment shall be validated against a UUID pattern so a crafted id cannot escape the backups directory; a malformed id → 400, an unknown id → 404.

verifiedBy.note: non-UUID id → 400 without touching the filesystem

requirements.title: GET /api/backups/download-all bundles every archive
requirements.text: GET /api/backups/download-all (admin) shall return a single ZIP containing every stored archive, each entry named by its descriptor fileName, so one download carries the whole backup history. The route shall be registered before /:id so the literal path is never taken for an id. With no backups stored it shall return 404.

requirements.title: Upload validates the archive before storing it
requirements.text: POST /api/backups/upload (admin) shall accept the archive as a raw octet-stream body (express.raw, mounted after the auth middleware so an unauthenticated body is never buffered) with the file name as a ?name= query parameter, and shall store it only after validation succeeds. Validation shall require a readable ZIP carrying a BrainGain manifest whose every listed data file is present and parses as JSON; anything else → 400 with a reason and nothing stored.

verifiedBy.note: non-ZIP, foreign-manifest and incomplete archives → 400, list unchanged

requirements.title: Restore is validated, undoable and all-or-nothing
requirements.text: POST /api/backups/:id/restore (admin) shall replace all application data with the archive contents and return { restored, files, materials, safetyBackupId }. It shall validate the archive fully BEFORE writing anything; take an automatic pre-restore backup of the current data first (source "pre-restore") so a wrong restore is undoable; stage the JSON stores and move them into place per file; and reconcile the materials directory to the archive contents. A rejected archive shall leave the dataset untouched and no staging directory behind. Backup and restore operations shall be serialized so two admin actions cannot interleave.

verifiedBy.note: changed data reverts; corrupt archive → 400 with the dataset unchanged

requirements.title: Archive scope is an allowlist — no TLS key, no nested backups
requirements.text: Archiving and restoring shall both work from one explicit allowlist (fileStore.STORE_FILES, from which the ArrayFile type is derived so a new store cannot be added without appearing in backups): the JSON stores users, roles, trainings, sessions, orgUnits and settings, plus the files in data/materials/. Consequently data/tls/ is never archived (the private key must never leave the server) and a restore never disturbs the running certificate, and data/backups/ is never archived (no self-inclusion) and survives a restore, so the backup list — including the pre-restore snapshot — remains available afterwards. Material files shall be taken from the directory listing rather than from the training descriptors, so orphaned uploads are preserved.

verifiedBy.note: archive entries contain no tls/ or PEM material and no nested backups/

requirements.title: Backup endpoints are admin-only
requirements.text: The /api/backups router shall apply authenticate + requireAdmin to every endpoint, so an anonymous caller gets 401 and a trainer or member 403 for list, create, download, download-all, upload, restore and delete. A backup is a complete dump of the dataset including password hashes, activation tokens and the stored SMTP password, and a restore overwrites everything — so no non-administrator may reach any of it, and no archive bytes are returned to a non-admin.

verifiedBy.note: every backup endpoint → 401 anonymous, 403 trainer/member

requirements.title: Backups admin page
requirements.text: An admin-only /backups page shall list the stored backups with archive name, creation date, size, contents summary and origin (manual, pre-restore, uploaded or automatic), offering per row Download, Restore and Delete plus page actions Create backup, Upload backup and Download all. Restore and Delete shall require an in-place confirmation, the page shall state what an archive contains and that the TLS key is excluded, and after a restore that no longer contains the signed-in account the client shall send the administrator back to the sign-in page. The route shall be gated by requiresAdmin and the sidebar link shown to administrators only.

requirements.title: Automatic backup scheduler & retention
requirements.text: Settings shall carry autoBackup { enabled (default false), intervalDays (integer, clamped 1..365, default 7), keep (integer, clamped 1..100, default 5) }, merged per-field by PUT /api/settings (admin). After the boot data migrations and then every hour, if automation is enabled and the newest backup with source 'auto' is older than intervalDays — or none exists — the server shall create a backup with source 'auto' (guarded against concurrent runs, fire-and-forget so boot is never delayed) and afterwards delete the oldest 'auto' backups beyond keep; manual, uploaded and pre-restore backups shall never be pruned. The Settings page shall present the schedule as its own card (enable toggle, interval-in-days and backups-to-keep inputs, own save button) and the Backups page shall label automatic backups in its source column.

verifiedBy.note: defaults + clamps round-trip; boot catch-up, retention and disabled paths via two-boot DATA_DIR tests
the Settings card round-trips the schedule across a reload

requirements.title: Append-only audit store & entry schema
requirements.text: The audit trail shall be an append-only NDJSON file (DATA_DIR/audit.ndjson) deliberately outside the fileStore STORE_FILES allowlist. Each line is one AuditEntry { id (UUID), timestamp (ISO 8601), actor { id, email, impersonatorId?, impersonatorEmail? } | null, action, entityType, entityId, entityName, changes?, details? }. Appends are serialized so concurrent requests never interleave partial lines; a failed append is logged to the console and never fails the business operation. Reading skips unparsable (torn) lines and returns no entries when the file does not exist yet.

verifiedBy.note: entries append across mutations; a torn last line is skipped on read

requirements.title: Administrative data mutations audited with redacted field diffs
requirements.text: Every create/update/delete of users (including committed import rows), roles, trainings (including reorder and material upload), organizational units (including member moves) and settings (including TLS certificate changes) shall append an audit entry naming the actor and entity; updates carry field-level before/after diffs computed by diffEntities/diffSettings. A user's roleIds diff lists each role as 'Name (id)' (labelIdList) so the entry reads without a lookup and stays meaningful after the role is renamed or deleted; an id that resolves to no role stays bare. The diff skips id/createdAt and masks secrets as '***' on both sides: passwordHash (reported as 'password'), activationToken, entraOid, a training's questions and its draft (both carry the answer key), and smtp.password (settings dot-path).

verifiedBy.note: user CRUD writes entries with diffs, role assignments labelled 'Name (id)' and a masked password; settings save diffs dot-paths and never logs the SMTP password; a training edit masks the question key

requirements.title: Authentication events audited
requirements.text: Successful password sign-ins, failed sign-ins (actor-less, recording only the attempted email and a generic reason), SSO sign-ins (plus a 'create' entry when a user is auto-provisioned and an 'update' entry when a Microsoft account is linked), account activation, and impersonation (naming the administrator as actor and the target user as entity) shall each append an audit entry.
