verifiedBy.note: login, failed login, activation and impersonation entries with the expected actors

requirements.title: Backup lifecycle and training completions audited
requirements.text: Backup creation (manual by the acting administrator; automatic runs actor-less with details 'automatic'), backup upload, backup deletion, a successful restore (with the safety backup id in the details) and a failed restore shall each append an audit entry. A passed grading run shall append a 'training-completed' entry with the learner as actor and the achieved score; failed attempts append nothing (they are not persisted anywhere by design).

verifiedBy.note: a passed grading writes an entry with the score, a failed one writes none; backup create/restore entries appear

requirements.title: Audit read API with filters and paging
requirements.text: GET /api/audit shall be administrator-only and return { total, entries } newest first, filtered server-side by action, entityType, free text q (case-insensitive over actor email, impersonator email, entity name, entity id and details) and inclusive from/to date bounds, paged by offset (default 0) and limit (default 50, clamped 1..500). total is the count after filtering.

verifiedBy.note: 401/403 for non-admins; filters and offset/limit paging round-trip

requirements.title: Audit CSV export
requirements.text: GET /api/audit/export.csv shall be administrator-only and stream the whole filtered trail (same filter parameters, no paging) as a CSV attachment: UTF-8 with BOM, CRLF line ends, RFC-4180 quoting, a formula-injection guard (cells starting with =, +, - or @ are prefixed with an apostrophe), header row timestamp/actorEmail/impersonatorEmail/action/entityType/entityId/entityName/changes/details, and changes flattened as 'field: from → to' pairs.

verifiedBy.note: attachment headers, header row, filtered rows, quoting and the formula guard

requirements.title: Audit log carried in backups but never restored
requirements.text: buildArchive shall include data/audit.ndjson in every backup ZIP and record it in the manifest's separate 'audit' field — never in 'files', which validateArchive maps against STORE_FILES and restoreBackup stages and swaps. A restore therefore never extracts or overwrites the local audit log; it survives every restore, and the restore itself (or its failure) is appended as a new entry afterwards.

verifiedBy.note: archive carries data/audit.ndjson outside manifest.files; entries written before a restore are still present afterwards plus the backup-restore entry

requirements.title: Admin audit trail page
requirements.text: The SPA shall provide an administrator-only Audit trail page (route /audit, guarded by requiresAdmin, sidebar entry in the admin block) that lists entries newest first with time, actor (with a 'via impersonator' badge and 'System' for actor-less entries), action badge, entity and details; a filter bar (action, entity type, debounced free text, from/to dates) mapped to the API's query parameters; an expandable per-row field/before/after diff table; offset/limit paging with an 'x–y of total' readout; and an Export CSV button downloading through the authorized client.

verifiedBy.note: admin sees, filters and expands entries and exports CSV; non-admins have no nav entry and are redirected

requirements.title: Materials confirmation audited
requirements.text: POST /api/sessions/confirm-materials (any authenticated learner, body { trainingId }) shall append a 'materials-confirmed' audit entry with the learner as actor, the training as entity and the number of provided materials in the details, and return 204; an unknown trainingId is a 404 and an unauthenticated call a 401 — neither writes an entry. The action appears in the audit page's action filter and badge set.

verifiedBy.note: the entry carries learner actor, training entity and material count; 404/401 paths write nothing

requirements.title: Answer key is a set of option indices
requirements.text: A question's answer key shall be correctIndices: number[] — every correct option, never empty. sanitizeQuestions shall normalize whatever a client sends into unique, in-bounds, ascending integers, accept a bare number (a legacy payload) as a one-element key, fall back to [0] when nothing usable remains, and never persist the legacy correctIndex field. For a multiple-choice question the training editor shall offer a checkbox per option and shall refuse to untick the last remaining correct answer; a single-choice question's key is edited as a radio group instead (see SYS-TRN-14).

verifiedBy.note: out-of-range/duplicate/unordered keys normalize; legacy scalar accepted

requirements.title: Grading is exact set match
requirements.text: Grading shall treat a question as correct only when the learner's selected option set equals the answer key exactly: no partial credit for a subset, and a superset (including ticking every option) is wrong. Selection order and duplicates shall not matter, and an empty selection shall be wrong rather than correct-by-default. The learner UI shall present every multiple-choice question as a multi-select (checkboxes) — the control type, not a textual prompt, signals that several answers may be right — so its number of correct answers is never disclosed — the public payload carries only { id, text, options, type }. A single-choice question discloses "exactly one" by design and is rendered as a radio group (see SYS-SES-06).

verifiedBy.note: subset and superset both score 0; order/duplicates irrelevant

requirements.title: Single-choice rendering and payload
requirements.text: toPublic shall emit a computed type on every learner-facing question — 'single' only when the stored type says so AND the answer key has exactly one entry, 'multiple' otherwise (including records without a type) — while still stripping the answer key itself. The learner UI shall render a single-choice question as a radio group (no textual prompt — the control type carries the semantics), where picking an option replaces the previous selection; the answer is still submitted as a one-element set, so exact set match grades an API-forged multi-selection against a single-choice question as wrong without special casing.

verifiedBy.note: public payload is { id, text, options, type }; a multi-selection against a single-choice question scores 0

requirements.title: A failed attempt optionally names the wrong questions
requirements.text: POST /api/sessions/grade shall include wrongIndices — the indices of the wrongly answered questions — in its response only when revealWrongQuestions is enabled AND the attempt failed; a passed attempt never carries the field, even when imperfect, and the response never contains the answer key or per-option detail. On a failed result the session page shall list the named questions by their text above the retry action.

verifiedBy.note: exact indices on fail when enabled; absent when off, on pass, and no key leaks

requirements.title: Session material language resolution
requirements.text: The session's material step shall follow the UI language (en/de) with no separate picker. Per material the current language's variant is shown; when it is missing the English variant stands in; when English is missing too, every variant is offered. Only variants NOT in the current language are marked — with the variant's language flag; a matching variant carries none.

verifiedBy.note: German user sees German material unadorned; English-only material carries its language flag

requirements.title: Quiz language resolution
requirements.text: The quiz step shall display each question's text and answer options in the session's chosen material language, resolving every string with the material logic — chosen language, then English, then all filled languages joined — and shall mark a question whose text is not available in the chosen language with the shown language's flag — including a single-language text that is neither the chosen language nor English; only a genuinely mixed joined value stays unflagged. Answers are submitted as option indices, so grading is identical whatever language was displayed.

verifiedBy.note: German learner sees German texts, the English-only question falls back with the English flag, and the quiz passes

requirements.title: Materials-confirmation gate & test-less completion
requirements.text: The session page's start action shall open a confirmation dialog stating that the learner is aware of all provided materials; cancelling returns to the material step unchanged, confirming first records the confirmation (POST /api/sessions/confirm-materials) and then starts the quiz. For a training without questions the start action shall stay enabled (learner-side startability requires material only — the trainer views keep flagging the missing test) and read as completing the training: after the confirmation the page submits an empty grading run, which passes at 100% (0 questions), persists the TrainingSession, and shows a completion message naming the confirmation instead of a 0-of-0 score.

verifiedBy.note: grading a question-less training passes at 100% and persists the session
dialog appears on start, cancel keeps the material step, confirming a test-less training completes it

requirements.title: Trainer contact card
requirements.text: GET /api/trainings/:id/trainer (any authenticated user) shall return the owning trainer's { name, email, orgUnitName } — and nothing else of the user record; an unknown training or a deleted owner account is a 404. The session page shall fetch the card best-effort and render the hint (label + name · org unit · mailto-linked email) inside the materials confirmation dialog and on the result screen for passed and failed attempts; when the card cannot be resolved the hint is simply hidden.

verifiedBy.note: returns exactly name/email/orgUnitName for the seeded trainer; 404 for unknown training; 401 anonymous
the hint with name, unit and email is visible in the dialog and on the failed result screen

requirements.title: Legacy single-answer questions are migrated
requirements.text: Questions stored in the previous single-answer shape (correctIndex: n) shall be migrated to correctIndices: [n] once, at boot, next to the org-unit migration, and the legacy field shall be removed. The migration shall be idempotent — a no-op when every question already carries the new field, so a normal start does not rewrite the store.

verifiedBy.note: a legacy scalar key normalizes and nothing legacy remains on disk

requirements.title: Localized materials data model & migration
requirements.text: Training.materials shall be sanitized on write against the fixed content languages (English and German): a variant's locale must be configured (else the variant is dropped), a variant holds exactly one content — an uploaded file (validated by UUID id, winning over a url) or a non-empty url — with empty variants dropped, at most one variant per locale (first wins, ordered by the settings list), a file variant with no label named after its file, and a material with no surviving variant dropped entirely (the ≥1-variant rule). Legacy materialLinks/materialFiles records shall be migrated idempotently to single-English-variant materials at boot and again after a backup restore, deleting the legacy fields.

verifiedBy.note: variants round-trip; unknown-locale/empty variants dropped; legacy shape migrates at boot

requirements.title: Localized question texts
requirements.text: Question.text and every entry of Question.options shall be per-language maps (locale → string) sanitized on write against the fixed content languages (English and German): unconfigured languages are dropped, a legacy plain string becomes the English entry, options empty in every language are removed with the answer key remapped to the surviving indices, and a question with no text in any language is dropped (the ≥1 rule). The option structure, answer key and question type stay language-independent, so grading never depends on the display language. Legacy plain-string records are migrated to English entries at boot and after a backup restore; the live bilingual strings were separated by hand into proper de/en entries.

verifiedBy.note: per-language round-trip; empty-option key remap; textless questions dropped; boot migration

requirements.title: Localized training master data model & migration
requirements.text: Training.name, Training.description and Training.category shall be per-language maps (locale → string) sanitized on write against the fixed content languages (English and German): unconfigured languages are dropped, a legacy plain string becomes the English entry, and a create whose sanitized name has no language is refused (400) — the ≥1-language rule applies to the name only. On update a present field is sanitized and an absent one keeps its stored value. Legacy plain-string records are migrated idempotently to English entries (an empty string to an empty map) at boot and again after a backup restore; the live bilingual strings were separated by hand into proper de/en entries.

verifiedBy.note: per-language round-trip; nameless create refused; legacy strings coerce; boot migration

requirements.title: Serialized store mutations & atomic writes
requirements.text: Every read-modify-write of a JSON store shall run inside fileStore.transaction() (or updateStore/updateSettings), which holds one process-wide, re-entrant store lock across the callback; plain reads need no lock. Every store, settings, marker, attempt and sidecar write shall go through temp+rename (writeJsonAtomic/writeFileAtomic) so a reader never observes a partial file and a crash never truncates one; temp files a crash left behind are swept at boot. The SCORM attempt index is written only through its own queue (updateAttemptIndex), lifecycle entry points (launch, grade) run inside a transaction, closeAttempt is a compare-and-set, and the resumed attempt file is loaded inside the attempt queue. Backup snapshots, the restore swap and the data migrations take the store lock (lock order: backup queue outside, store lock inside). GET /api/trainings never writes; the order backfill is a boot migration.

implementedBy.symbol: grade: consume attempt + write session in one transaction

verifiedBy.note: parallel writers (users, sessions, acks, trainings), double grade, double launch, atomic files

requirements.title: Async handler error containment
requirements.text: A rejected or thrown async route handler shall be answered with a JSON 500 through the error middleware and shall never terminate the process: every route module uses asyncRouter() (a Router whose handlers forward rejections to next(err)), the SCORM content handler is wrapped the same way, the error middleware defers to Express when headers were already sent, and an unhandledRejection that escapes everything is logged instead of exiting.

verifiedBy.note: torn store file → 500 JSON; /api/health still 200

requirements.title: Training editor dialog structure
requirements.text: The training editor shall be a modal dialog (role="dialog", aria-modal, closed by Escape or the scrim with the draft discarded, at most ~896px wide and 88vh tall, with the record title as its heading and Save/Cancel/Delete in a footer). Its body shall be four collapsible sections — Basics, Schedule, Learning material, Quiz questions — each with a header carrying the section title and a summary of its contents (an empty section is flagged), and only Basics open when the dialog opens. Each question shall itself be collapsible, shown while closed as its text plus an option/correct-answer count. Anything the author adds shall open itself: a new question expands, and uploading a file or adding a link opens its section. Collapsed bodies shall be hidden, not unmounted, so state and the file picker survive folding.

verifiedBy.note: only Basics expanded on open; summaries report hidden content; a new question expands

requirements.title: Question type
requirements.text: A question shall carry type: 'single' | 'multiple'. A record without the field (saved before it existed, or restored from a backup) shall behave as 'multiple' everywhere; sanitizeQuestions shall persist the type explicitly on every save and shall coerce 'single' to 'multiple' whenever the answer key does not have exactly one entry, never rejecting the request. The training editor shall offer the type switch per question, enable switching to single-choice only while exactly one answer is correct, edit a single-choice key as a radio group where picking an option replaces the previous one, and start a newly added question as single-choice.

verifiedBy.note: type round-trips; single with several correct answers is coerced to multiple; absent type reads as multiple

requirements.title: Per-language material authoring
requirements.text: The training editor's material section shall show one sub-card per material with one row per content language (English and German) — each row prefixed by the language's flag alone (no code label), with a per-language label and a web-link input or an uploaded-file chip with a per-row upload action. Languages left blank are simply not offered — the server drops them on save — and the collapsed section summary shall report the material count plus the languages that carry content (e.g. "2 materials · EN DE").

verifiedBy.note: EN+DE variants of one material round-trip; summary reports both languages

requirements.title: Per-language question authoring
requirements.text: The training editor shall offer one flag-prefixed input (flag only, no code label) per content language (English and German) for a question's text and for every answer option, while the option rows themselves — add/remove, the correct-answer key and the question type — are shared across languages. Languages left blank are dropped on save.

verifiedBy.note: EN+DE question and answers round-trip into their language rows

requirements.title: Per-language training basics & resolved display
requirements.text: The training editor's Basics section shall offer one flag-prefixed input (flag only, no code label) per content language (English and German) for the name, category and description — blank languages are dropped on save. Everywhere these fields are displayed (dashboard cards, the trainings list and its editor dialog title, the session header, trainee groups and reminder mail texts, My Team rows, role checkbox labels, and the Training Plan / Training Status Report PDFs) the value shall be resolved to the user's language with the shared per-string logic — chosen language, then English, then every filled language joined — without the alternative-language flag, which stays a session-page affordance. Search boxes shall match every language of a localized field, and alphabetical sorting shall use the resolved value.

implementedBy.symbol: resolved rows/dialog title, blankTraining localized maps

verifiedBy.note: EN+DE name rows round-trip in the editor; a German member sees the German name on the dashboard card

requirements.title: Training update data model
requirements.text: Training carries `version` (number, 0 = never published), `updates` (append-only TrainingUpdate[]: id, publishedAt, deadline normalized to end-of-day UTC, mode retake|confirm, optional note, publishedBy, version) and `draft?` (the staged WIP content — see SYS-UPD-07). `version` and `updates` are SERVER-MANAGED like `order`: PUT /api/trainings/:id never reads them from the body; the published materials/questions are written exclusively by publish-update, PUT staging content into the draft only. Confirm-mode acknowledgements live in their own store file `updateAcks` (UpdateAck: id, userId, trainingId, updateId, confirmedAt) listed in ARRAY_FILES so backup/restore covers it. Boot/post-restore migrations backfill version 1 on legacy records WITHOUT the field (never coercing an explicit 0) and prune acknowledgements whose training, update or user no longer exists.

requirements.title: POST /api/trainings/:id/publish-update
requirements.text: POST /api/trainings/:id/publish-update (admin or owning trainer) accepts kind 'notify' (default) or 'silent' (see SYS-UPD-08 for the kinds and promotion). For notify it validates mode ('retake'|'confirm'), deadline (a calendar day, today or later, stored as end-of-day UTC) and non-empty emailSubject/emailText (composed client-side from i18n, editable in the publish dialog); 404 for an unknown training. It promotes an existing draft, increments the training version, appends the update stamped with that version, resolves the affected users (role-assigned AND at least one pass) and BCC-emails the non-disabled ones via the SMTP service. An unconfigured SMTP, zero recipients or a send failure NEVER fails the publish — the 201 response reports { update, version, affected, email: sent|skipped|failed }. Audited as 'training-update-published' with version, kind, mode, deadline and counts in the details.

requirements.title: computeDue() 'updated' overlay
requirements.text: computeDue(training, sessions, acks, now) extends the cycle computation with a DueStatus 'updated': applied ONLY when the cycle is otherwise 'up-to-date' (never/due/overdue take precedence — a new pass postdates every publish and satisfies all updates). An update is pending when publishedAt > lastPassedAt and, for confirm mode, no acknowledgement exists; among several the earliest deadline governs (tie → newest publish). The result carries dueDate = the governing update's deadline and the pendingUpdate payload; past the deadline the status stays 'updated' (the client renders it overdue-styled). All three due views (/trainings/mine, /trainings/trainees, /org-units/my-team) pass the caller's acknowledgements.

requirements.title: Update acknowledgements (confirm mode)
requirements.text: POST /api/sessions/confirm-materials accepts an optional updateId: it persists an UpdateAck for the calling user (idempotent — a repeat records nothing new), audited as 'training-update-confirmed'. Only confirm-mode updates are acknowledgeable: an unknown updateId is 404 and a retake-mode update is 400 (a confirmation never clears a retake). Without updateId the endpoint behaves exactly as before. Acknowledgements are removed when their update is withdrawn or their training deleted; the prune migration is the safety net after a restore.

implementedBy.symbol: ack cleanup in DELETE /:id and DELETE /:id/updates/:updateId

requirements.title: DELETE /api/trainings/:id/updates/:updateId
requirements.text: DELETE /api/trainings/:id/updates/:updateId (admin or owning trainer) withdraws a published update: it is removed from the training, its acknowledgements are pruned, and the action is audited as 'training-update-cancelled' naming the withdrawn version. The training version is NOT decremented. Unknown training or update → 404.

requirements.title: Version lifecycle
requirements.text: A training version starts at 0 = never published (POST /api/trainings initializes it; legacy records without the field are backfilled to 1 at boot — their live content IS the published content — and an explicit 0 is never coerced). Each publish — silent ones included — sets version = current + 1 (the first publish creates version 1), stamps `publishedAt` on the training (the date of the last update; server-managed like the version, absent on legacy records where it is unknown) and, for notify publishes, stamps the new version on the update record. Withdrawing an update or discarding a draft never decrements the version or touches publishedAt — numbers are never reused. The trainings list shows "Version {N} · {publish date}" (the word written out, never a "v{N}" shorthand) on its own line right below the training name (no version while unpublished — the "Not published yet" pill flags that; the version alone when the date is unknown), the publish dialog announces the version a publish will create, and the training editor shows the current version right after its title (the Versions button itself carries no number). Learner-facing views show no version numbers: the dashboard card (which says "in preparation" while unpublished), the session page and the session's update banner carry none — versions are a trainer-side concept.

requirements.title: Draft model & content staging
requirements.text: Training carries `draft?: { materials, questions, savedAt }` — a complete WIP snapshot. POST /api/trainings creates version 0 with empty published content and routes any body content into the draft. PUT /api/trainings/:id applies metadata immediately but STAGES content: body materials/questions are sanitized (present-or-keep against the WIP), compared to the published content — equal clears the draft, different writes it (an unchanged draft keeps its savedAt, so a metadata-only save stays silent); the published fields are never written by PUT, and a client-supplied `draft` object is ignored. toPublic() strips `draft` from every learner payload (GET /, /mine, /:id for non-owners); owner/admin reads keep it. The audit diff masks `draft` wholesale (it carries the answer key). The boot/post-restore version migration backfills only records WITHOUT a version and never coerces an explicit 0 upward. Draft-referenced file bytes remain downloadable by id (unguessable UUIDs — the same exposure as replaced files before this feature).

implementedBy.symbol: openTraining() draft overlay, save() draft trigger

requirements.title: Publish kinds, promotion & version-0 gating
requirements.text: POST /:id/publish-update accepts kind 'notify' (default — backward compatible) or 'silent'. Both promote an existing draft into the published fields, bump the version (0→1 first), clear the draft and delete published file bytes the promotion superseded. 'silent' appends no update, sends no email, responds { version } and is refused (400) without a draft; 'notify' keeps the existing obligation/email behavior and is refused (400) at version 0 (nobody can have completed an unpublished training, and update records are v2+). POST /api/sessions/grade refuses an unpublished training with 409 BEFORE the zero-questions auto-pass, persisting nothing; confirm-materials stays evidence-only (it persists nothing without an updateId). Audit details carry `version=N kind=notify|silent`.

requirements.title: DELETE /api/trainings/:id/draft
requirements.text: DELETE /api/trainings/:id/draft (admin or owning trainer) discards the WIP: the draft is removed (404 when none exists), file bytes only the draft referenced are deleted (published bytes never), and the action is audited as 'training-draft-discarded'. Deleting a training removes the union of its published and draft file bytes.

requirements.title: Completion signature on /grade
requirements.text: Every POST /api/sessions/grade submission carries `reauth`: { password } verified with bcrypt against the ACTING user's passwordHash, or { entraIdToken } — a Microsoft ID token run through the full Entra verification chain, bound to the acting user's linked entraOid and refused when issued more than 5 minutes ago (the client forces a fresh interactive login via prompt:'login'). A missing or failed signature returns 403 (not 401 — the session itself stays valid and must not be bounced to login), grades nothing, and appends a 'login-failed' audit entry naming the acting account and the rejection reason. A verified signature is recorded on the 'training-completed' entry as 'signed: password|microsoft'. The UI collects the signature in a dialog before every quiz submission and inside the materials-confirmation dialog when that confirmation completes a test-less training; the identity payload exposes hasPassword so the dialog offers the right method.

requirements.title: Content reordering (editor + order persistence)
requirements.text: The training editor offers up/down move buttons on every material panel, question row and answer-option row (disabled at the ends). Moving an option remaps correctIndices for the two swapped positions, so the key keeps marking the same answers; moving a question keeps its expanded state. Server-side, materials[], questions[] and options[] persist exactly in the order given — through the draft staging (PUT), the publish promotion and every learner payload — and index-based grading works against the arranged order.

requirements.title: In-app material viewer: whole client area, one title line, full-tab toggle
requirements.text: frontend/src/utils/embed.ts decides what BrainGain renders itself. UPLOADED FILES are rendered by the app: a PDF through pdf.js page images (so it displays even when the browser is configured to download PDFs, and never enters a same-origin frame), text inline, media through a blob: URL in a native element — the bytes are fetched with the Authorization header, which an <iframe>/<video> cannot send on its own; HTML and SVG uploads are deliberately NOT renderable and stay downloads. LINKS are embedded only when the URL points straight at a document/media file: SharePoint/OneDrive sharing links (/:b:/, /:v:/, …, ?web=1) and pages are excluded because they serve authenticated viewer pages that send X-Frame-Options, which script cannot detect — a framed refusal is silently blank. A framed link is sandboxed without allow-top-navigation, granted allow-same-origin only when cross-origin, labelled third-party, and always offers the original URL. ContentViewer.vue renders one title line (training title, content controls, full-tab toggle) and switches the SAME element between the client area and fixed/inset-0 full tab by class — re-creating it would reload the content and, for SCORM, lose the running attempt. The page claims the client area through stores/layout.ts (no shared measure, no padding, no page scroll) and MUST release it again. The title line has three regions — title (left, truncating), the centred icon-only control group in reading order, status (right) — every control carrying both title and aria-label so tooltip and assistive tech read the same words. The completion control is always present but disabled until the course reported a result AND every write is acknowledged, its tooltip naming whichever is missing; "start over" confirms before discarding progress.

requirements.title: Import a SCORM course as training content
requirements.text: A trainer shall decide a training’s content type when setting it up: learning material plus the built-in quiz, OR an imported SCORM course (a SCORM 1.2 or 2004 .zip exported from an authoring tool) — the editor offers inputs for exactly one of the two, never both. The upload is staged like every other content edit — into the training’s draft — and reaches learners only when published. Switching the type is reversible (stored content is kept server-side and returns when switching back), but a training never mixes the two.

requirements.title: Run the imported course inside the app
requirements.text: A learner shall run the imported course inside BrainGain — embedded in the session page, not opened in a separate tab — with the app acting as the course’s LMS: it serves the content, answers the SCORM API, and receives the course’s progress and result. Opening a SCORM training starts the course immediately — there is no start step and no materials-awareness confirmation (SR-162 concerns provided materials; a SCORM training has none, the course itself is the content and the recorded attempt is the evidence). Any obligation the learner must know about (a pending update’s deadline and the trainer’s note) is shown as a slim banner above the course. Only single-SCO packages are supported; multi-lesson packages are refused at import.

requirements.title: Imported course content is isolated from the application
requirements.text: Imported course files are untrusted third-party HTML/JavaScript. They shall be delivered from a separate origin (a second HTTPS listener) and executed in a sandboxed iframe, so package script can never read the signed-in session (the API token), the application DOM, or act as the user; bridge messages from the content are validated by origin, source window, per-launch nonce, schema and sequence before they are touched, and a forged message can never produce a completion record.

requirements.title: Course progress and resume data are stored server-side
requirements.text: The course’s progress — status, score, bookmark position and suspend data — shall be stored server-side per attempt, so the learner resumes at the same point after signing out, changing device, or a browser crash. Suspend data round-trips byte-exact (authoring tools depend on it); an over-limit write is rejected with the SCORM error code, never truncated. A new package build or training version starts a fresh attempt — suspend data is specific to one build.

requirements.title: A SCORM completion is recorded through the identity re-confirmation
requirements.text: A SCORM course’s completion shall be recorded as a training session only after the learner re-confirms their identity at that moment (the SR-173 completion signature). The score and verdict are taken exclusively from the SERVER-held attempt the course reported into — no score, status or passed flag is ever accepted from the browser — the course’s own failed verdict vetoes, the organization’s pass threshold applies as the floor, and an attempt yields at most one session (replay is refused). The decision inputs are recorded in the audit trail.

requirements.title: Unsupported or unsafe packages are refused with a reason
requirements.text: Packages that are not usable — not a ZIP, no or ambiguous manifest, multi-SCO, unsupported SCORM versions, cmi5/xAPI packages, missing or non-HTML launch files — and archives that are unsafe — path traversal, symbolic links, encrypted entries, too many files, zip bombs — shall be refused at import with a stable, human-readable reason, leaving nothing on disk. The content origin serves package bytes only under a live, attempt-bound launch token and carries the isolation response headers; both origins send a Content-Security-Policy.

requirements.title: Replacing a course is a retake obligation
requirements.text: Replacing a training’s SCORM package is a content change like any other: it is staged in the draft, published explicitly, and announced as an update. For a SCORM-backed training the confirm-only update mode shall be refused — new course content must actually be run, not confirmed away — and the published package build is pinned to the version: attempts already running finish on the build they launched with.

requirements.title: Course files and attempt evidence are backed up and retained
requirements.text: Imported package files (with their directory structure preserved), in-progress attempt data, and the attempt behind every recorded completion shall be part of backup and restore. An attempt consumed by a recorded session is completion evidence and is never deleted by cleanup; unreferenced packages, crashed-import remnants and long-idle open attempts are swept automatically.

requirements.title: Learning material is viewed inside the app, using the whole client area
requirements.text: Learning material the browser can render — an uploaded PDF, text, image, video or audio file, or a link pointing straight at such a file — shall be shown INSIDE BrainGain, filling the whole client area, instead of being handed to a new tab or the downloads folder. The viewer shall carry the training title on the left, EVERY control centred as icons with tooltip labels (leave, start over, download, open externally, full tab, and last the completion action — the only one with a visible word, because it is the audited step), and status on the right, all in ONE title line. Progress status shall keep its words; content badges are icons. The original way out shall always remain available (download for a file, the URL for a link), and a control that discards the learner’s progress shall confirm first. Material only its own host can render — an authenticated document viewer, a page that refuses to be displayed inside another page — shall keep opening in a new tab, where it works.

requirements.title: SCORM data model & stores
requirements.text: SCORM state lives in two new array stores plus two byte trees: `scormPackages` (immutable-after-import descriptors: version, entry href, mastery score, trainer options) and `scormAttempts` (a denormalized index of attempts, written on lifecycle transitions only), with package files extracted to DATA_DIR/scorm/<packageId>/ preserving the archive’s ORIGINAL relative paths, and each attempt’s authoritative cmi in DATA_DIR/scorm-attempts/<attemptId>.json written via temp+rename. resolveScormEntry() is the single containment check for every path into a package tree — used at import, at serve time and at restore. Training/TrainingDraft reference a package by id only (server-resolved, never trusted as an object); TrainingSession carries the consuming attempt id as completion evidence.

requirements.title: Package upload, options and attachment
requirements.text: POST /api/trainings/scorm-packages (trainer/admin, raw zip bytes ≤ 500 MB, name as a query param) imports a package — fully validated and extracted before anything is recorded — and returns the descriptor; rejects are 422 { error, code, details } with a stable code, and both outcomes are audited (scorm-imported / scorm-rejected). PATCH …/:packageId edits exactly the two trainer options (completionRule, allowExternal); DELETE removes only unreferenced packages. A package attaches to a training via the id in PUT/POST trainings (staged into the draft); one package belongs to at most one training.

requirements.title: Manifest parsing, version detection and the single-SCO rule
requirements.text: imsmanifest.xml is parsed with a namespace-tolerant XML parser (no DTD/external-entity processing); elements/attributes are matched by local name because prefixes are arbitrary. The SCORM version is detected from schemaversion, then namespaces, then sequencing presence (defaulting to 1.2); SCORM 1.1/AICC are refused. The default organization’s item tree yields the SCOs: exactly one is required — multi-SCO packages are REFUSED (never silently reduced, which would create false completion records) — and its href (with xml:base applied) must exist in the archive and be an HTML page. adlcp:masteryscore (1.2, /100) or minNormalizedMeasure (2004) is stored normalized 0–1 as ADVISORY data. A manifest nested exactly one folder deep is accepted (that folder becomes the package root); cmi5/tincan packages are named as such in the rejection. In the editor the content type is an explicit choice: the SCORM section and the material/quiz sections are mutually exclusive — quiz and material inputs are never offered beside a course (stored content is kept server-side; switching the type back restores them, and removing the package falls back to the classic type).

requirements.title: Draft staging, publish promotion and version pinning
requirements.text: The staged package id participates in the draft/publish lifecycle exactly like materials/questions: PUT stages it (present-or-keep; explicit null detaches), the editor’s draft-change detection INCLUDES it (so a replaced package offers the publish dialog), publish-update promotes draft.scormPackageId into the published field and pins that build to the version, and replaced/detached packages are deleted once nothing references them. In-flight attempts keep running against the build they launched with; grading refuses an attempt whose package was superseded.

requirements.title: The content origin
requirements.text: Package files are served by a second HTTPS listener (SCORM_CONTENT_PORT, default 3012, same certificate — the TLS hot-swap re-keys every registered listener) whose express app imports no auth middleware and no route modules: /api/* answers 404 by construction, no cookie is ever set, no CORS header is ever sent. It serves exactly the wrapper page, the SCORM API shim and package files (streamed from disk with Range support) under /s/<launchToken>/… — the token in the URL PATH so relative asset resolution carries it. The player renders the launch URL in an iframe with sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-forms allow-modals allow-popups allow-downloads" (no allow-top-navigation — frame-busting is blocked; allow-same-origin is safe because the frame is on a DIFFERENT origin than the app) and referrerpolicy=no-referrer; the client refuses to launch if the content origin equals the app origin (the one deployment mistake that would void the isolation). The wrapper page and the SCORM API shim live in backend/src/scorm/shim/ and are read from <dist>/scorm/shim/ at runtime, so the backend build (npm run build) copies every non-TypeScript source asset (never src/data) into dist/ after tsc — a compiled deployment without that step answers every wrapper request with a 500 and no course can start.

requirements.title: Launch token and bridge validation
requirements.text: POST /api/sessions/scorm/launch mints an HS256 token signed with a key DERIVED from JWT_SECRET (unusable as an app bearer token, and vice versa), bound to { attempt, package, user } with an 8 h expiry — it authorizes BYTES only, never state: every cmi write goes to the main origin under the learner’s own JWT. The content server re-checks the attempt on every request (2 s cache), so the URL is revoked the moment the attempt closes. Bridge messages pass six checks in order — exact event.origin, exact source window, schema+caps, per-launch nonce, attemptId, monotonic seq — then the window listener is replaced by a MessagePort; outbound messages always name the exact targetOrigin. Payload caps: ≤512 keys, ≤65536 chars/value, ≤256 KB/batch; keys must match the cmi grammar and prototype-polluting names are rejected. The frontend protocol module is a hand-mirrored twin of the backend’s, held identical by a drift test.

requirements.title: The cmi model and the synchronous-read invariant
requirements.text: One version-neutral cmi model backs both dialects, mapped by a single table in both directions (1.2 lesson_status ↔ 2004 completion_status+success_status; a 1.2 read NEVER returns a value outside the 1.2 vocabulary). THE INVARIANT A MAINTAINER MUST NOT BREAK: the launch response ships the COMPLETE flattened cmi seed and the wrapper creates the SCO’s iframe only after the seed arrived — every LMSGetValue is answered locally on the same tick; no read ever crosses a frame or network boundary. Writes are buffered and flushed (Commit/Terminate/pagehide), never blocking. suspend_data is capped at 65536 chars for BOTH dialects (Storyline exceeds the 1.2 spec’s 4096 and needs byte-exact read-back); over-cap writes are rejected with the dialect’s SCORM error code, never truncated. total_time is SERVER-accumulated from session_time growth (no double-counting) and formatted per dialect; scores normalize to 0–1 (2004 scaled native, 1.2 derived from raw/min/max, guarding max=min); interactions/objectives/vendor elements are kept verbatim as capped evidence maps with _count synthesized; unknown reads return "" + error 401 (throwing breaks Captivate).

requirements.title: Attempt persistence and the commit endpoint
requirements.text: POST /api/sessions/scorm/attempts/:id/commit persists a batch of raw SCORM element writes WRITE-THROUGH: a 200 means the attempt file is durably on disk (temp+rename), which is what makes the player’s save indicator and the never-sign-unpersisted-evidence rule honest. Commits are owner-only (404 for anyone else — no existence oracle), re-validated against the payload caps, per-attempt rate-limited (429 on floods), serialized per attempt id, and refused with 409 once the attempt is closed or consumed — a finished attempt is immutable. The client coalesces writes (~2 s debounce), retries failed flushes with backoff without ever dropping a batch before a 2xx, and flushes on visibilitychange/pagehide via fetch keepalive (trimming to the completion-relevant subset when over the keepalive budget).

requirements.title: Resume and restart rules
requirements.text: launch resumes the newest open attempt matching (user, training, package, training version) — seeding entry=resume and the stored suspend data — and otherwise starts fresh (ab-initio). Attempts against a superseded package build or training version are never resumed (suspend data is build-specific) and are abandoned; restart=true explicitly abandons the open attempt and starts over. Trainer/admin trial runs and anything launched inside an impersonation session are PREVIEW attempts: mode=browse, credit=no-credit, never consumable into a session.

requirements.title: The SCORM grading arm
requirements.text: POST /api/sessions/grade accepts { trainingId, scormAttemptId, reauth } for a SCORM-backed training — the client names the attempt and NOTHING else. The endpoint validates ownership (404), training/package binding, preview (409), replay (consumed → 409) and superseded builds (409); forces a final flush and judges from the attempt FILE (never the index); requires the attempt to be completion-worthy under the package’s rule (else 409); verifies the SR-173 signature identically to the quiz path; computes the score exclusively server-side (scaled score, else 1 for a completion-only course — mirroring the quiz’s zero-questions rule); applies the course’s failed verdict as a VETO and Settings.passThreshold as the FLOOR (the manifest masteryScore is NOT re-applied — the SCO already graded itself with it); persists the session with the attempt id and closes the attempt as consumed on pass, or closes it as failed (nothing persisted) so a relaunch starts ab-initio. The audit detail records score, dialect, verdict, mastery, threshold, rule, time, attempt and signature method.

requirements.title: Completion rules and the mutual-exclusion guards
requirements.text: The trainer-chosen completionRule gates when grading may run, SERVER-side: status (the course reported a definitive verdict — passed, failed or completed), exit (a clean Terminate suffices — for courses that never report completion), or time (the training’s duration of SERVER-clocked in-content activity — capped inter-commit deltas, never a client-reported total_time). Quiz answers and SCORM attempts are mutually exclusive in both directions: POST /api/sessions/grade REFUSES answers[] for a SCORM-backed training with 409 (closing the zero-questions auto-pass hole) and scormAttemptId for a quiz training with 400. Confirm-mode updates are refused for SCORM-backed trainings at publish AND at acknowledgement — new course content must be run, not clicked away.

requirements.title: Security response headers on both origins
requirements.text: The app origin sends a strict CSP (script-src self; frame-src limited to the content origin; frame-ancestors none — report-only by default, enforced with CSP_ENFORCE=1) plus X-Frame-Options DENY, nosniff, Referrer-Policy no-referrer, Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy same-origin-allow-popups (plain same-origin would break the MSAL re-auth popup on the SR-173 critical path) and a deny-by-default Permissions-Policy; CORS is an explicit allowlist (the content origin is deliberately NOT on it). The content origin’s CSP is permissive about EXECUTING (authoring output needs inline script and eval — isolation comes from the origin boundary and the sandbox) but restrictive about EGRESS: connect-src self blocks exfiltration, widened to https: only by the per-package allowExternal option; frame-ancestors names the app origin and self (the wrapper frames the SCO); the CSP sandbox directive is byte-identical to the player’s iframe attribute (one shared constant, asserted end-to-end); Referrer-Policy no-referrer keeps the launch token out of Referer.

requirements.title: Archive validation guards
requirements.text: Import validates every entry BEFORE anything touches the filesystem: path length/depth caps, entry-count cap (2000), rejection of absolute/drive/UNC/dot-segment/control-character paths and symbolic links, per-entry (200 MB) and total (500 MB) uncompressed caps re-checked DURING extraction (a lying central directory cannot get past the census), a compression-ratio bomb guard, and encrypted-entry rejection. On any failure the half-extracted tree is deleted — an import either completes or leaves nothing. resolveScormEntry() re-guards every serve-time and restore-time path.

requirements.title: Backup, restore, GC and retention
requirements.text: Backups archive package trees under data/scorm/<packageId>/… with their ORIGINAL relative paths (unlike materials these cannot be basename-flattened) and attempt files under data/scorm-attempts/; both prefixes are optional in an archive, so pre-SCORM backups restore unchanged. Restore writes package entries only after UUID-validating the package segment and passing resolveScormEntry — a hostile path in an uploaded archive is skipped, never written — then prunes what the archive does not contain. gcScorm() runs with the boot/restore migrations: it sweeps unreferenced package records past a grace period, recordless trees (crashed imports), attempts whose training or package is gone, and abandons long-idle open attempts — and NEVER touches a consumed attempt or its file (completion evidence).

requirements.title: Training card preview image
requirements.text: A trainer shall be able to give a training a preview image that is shown as the cover of the learner’s training card on the dashboard (image on top, the due status flush in the cover’s corner, title, category, description, cycle/duration line and Start button below, as before). Any training without an image keeps the same card shape with its category tint and a neutral glyph in place of the picture, so a dashboard with and without images stays evenly gridded. The image is master data like the name: it takes effect on save without a publish step and never triggers a content-update obligation. Only raster images (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF) are accepted; the editor scales the picture down before upload so payloads and backups stay small. No SCORM or LOM element defines a cover image, so an imported course package is scanned for one by vendor convention (Articulate Storyline’s meta.xml thumbnail, then conventionally named image files); when a candidate exists the editor shows the picture and OFFERS it as the preview image — the trainer decides, and nothing is applied without their click. The same choice stays available whenever the training is edited: next to the local upload, the editor offers “Use image from course package” for as long as a package with a cover picture is attached, so a trainer can switch to (or back to) the package picture at any time.

requirements.title: Training preview image: storage, validation, delivery & cleanup
requirements.text: Training.previewImage is an optional { id, name, size, type } descriptor of an upload made through POST /api/trainings/materials (the shared byte store, so backups cover it). POST /api/trainings and PUT /api/trainings/:id shall validate a supplied descriptor against the STORED sidecar — UUID id, an existing upload, type in {image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp, image/gif}, size ≤ 5 MB — rebuilding the persisted descriptor from the sidecar (a client-claimed type is ignored) and answering 400 otherwise; PUT applies present-or-keep (absent = keep, null = remove). The field is master data: it is written immediately, never staged into the draft, and changes neither version nor publish state. Learner payloads carry the descriptor (toPublic keeps master data); the client fetches GET /api/trainings/materials/:fileId with the Authorization header and renders a blob: URL, because an cannot authenticate. Bytes are deleted when the image is replaced or removed (unless a material still references the id) and when the training is deleted. The frontend scales the picked image to fit 800 × 450 and re-encodes it as JPEG before upload (transparent areas on white).

verifiedBy.note: descriptor stored and delivered to learners; non-image / forged descriptors 400; replace/remove/delete free the bytes; no draft or version change

requirements.title: SCORM package cover candidate (thumbnailHref) & inline thumbnail route
requirements.text: At import, services/scorm/import.ts records ScormPackageRef.thumbnailHref — a POSIX-relative cover-image CANDIDATE — read from vendor conventions in this order: Articulate Storyline’s meta.xml at the package root (`<project thumburl="…">`, parsed with fast-xml-parser, ≤ 256 KB, BOM tolerated), then the shallowest conventionally named image entry (thumbnail|thumb|poster|cover|preview with a raster extension). A candidate must be an existing package entry with a raster extension (png/jpg/jpeg/webp/gif — never SVG), pass the same containment check as every other entry (resolveScormEntry), and stay ≤ 5 MB once inflated; otherwise the next candidate is tried and the field is omitted when none qualifies. GET /api/trainings/scorm-packages/:packageId/thumbnail (trainer/admin) serves the candidate’s bytes inline with the content type derived from the extension, nosniff, 404 when the package has none. The editor fetches it with the Authorization header, shows the picture next to the manifest card with “Use as preview image” / “Not now”, and on use downsizes the bytes client-side and uploads them through POST /materials like a picked file, so the same preview-image validation applies. The offer is hidden once the training has a preview image and is dismissable per editing session; nothing is applied without the trainer’s click. Independently of the offer, the Basics preview-image block renders a “Use image from course package” action (testid preview-image-from-scorm) whenever the attached package carries a thumbnailHref whose bytes could be fetched — visible while editing an existing training too, with or without a current preview image — running the same client-side downsize + upload. thumbnailHref is always written by the import (a path, or null when nothing qualifies); records that predate the field (key absent) are backfilled once at boot and after a backup restore by migrateScormThumbnails (services/scorm/thumbnail.ts), which scans the extracted package directory with the same rules — so packages imported by an earlier release offer their cover too.

requirements.title: Identifiable release version
requirements.text: Every installation shall report the exact application version it runs. The version shall be a single semantic MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH number recorded once in the repository and carried into the package descriptors and the SBOMs, so the version a user sees, the version a monitor probes and the version the SBOM describes are the same number.

requirements.title: Automatic, once-only data upgrades
requirements.text: Installing a newer version over an existing data directory shall bring the stored data up to date automatically when the server starts, applying each version’s data migration exactly once and recording what was done, so an administrator upgrades by deploying the new release and restarting — never by editing data.

requirements.title: A recovery point before data is changed
requirements.text: Before the first data-changing migration of an upgrade the application shall create a restorable backup automatically, and shall create none when no migration is due, so a faulty upgrade can be undone from the application’s own backups.

requirements.title: Downgrade protection
requirements.text: The application shall refuse to operate on data written by a newer version than itself, stating both versions and the way back, so an older build can never silently drop or corrupt records it does not understand. An explicit, documented emergency override shall exist for operators.

requirements.title: Version-aware restore
requirements.text: Restoring a backup shall bring the archive’s data to the running version’s shape regardless of the version that produced it, and an archive from a newer version shall be refused with a clear message and no change to the current data.

requirements.title: Documented release history
requirements.text: Every release shall be documented in a human-readable changelog naming its data migrations, and identified by a repository tag, so an operator can tell what changed between the deployed version and a newer one before upgrading.

requirements.title: Concurrent use never loses or corrupts a record
requirements.text: The system shall be safe for many users acting at the same moment: two requests that write at the same time shall both persist (no lost update), a completion or acknowledgement confirmed to a learner shall be on disk, a SCORM attempt shall yield at most one completion even when submitted twice at once, a stored file shall never be observed or left half-written, and one failing request shall never take the server down for the other users.

requirements.title: Root VERSION file is the single version source of truth
requirements.text: The application version shall be the content of the repository’s root VERSION file, strict MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. tools/sync-version.mjs shall copy it into package.json, backend/package.json, frontend/package.json, both package-lock.json files (root and packages[""]) and requirements.json meta.version (written through the shared serializer); the SBOMs shall report it as metadata.component.version. npm run verify shall fail when any descriptor disagrees (sync-version.mjs --check).

verifiedBy.note: VERSION, both package.json, both lockfiles, meta.version and the SBOM root component agree

requirements.title: Version exposure: GET /api/health, GET /api/version and the About dialog
requirements.text: GET /api/health (unauthenticated) shall return { ok: true, version } where version is the app version. GET /api/version (admin only; 401 without a token, 403 for a non-admin) shall return { app, data, migratedAt, history } from the data-version marker. The user menu shall offer an About dialog, available to every authenticated user, showing the app version; an admin shall additionally see the data version.

verifiedBy.note: health carries version; /api/version 200 for admin, 403 for member, 401 anonymous; About dialog shows both

requirements.title: Data-version marker DATA_DIR/_meta.json
requirements.text: The backend shall keep DATA_DIR/_meta.json = { app, dataVersion, appVersion, migratedAt, history[] } (history oldest first, capped at 50 entries of { version, at, action, changed?, note? }), written atomically via temp+rename. Before seeding, a data directory without a marker shall be stamped at the app version when no store file exists (action "initialized") and adopted at the baseline 1.2.0 when stores exist (action "adopted"). A marker that exists but is unusable shall be reported and treated as absent, never fatal. The marker shall not be a STORE_FILES store and shall not be swapped by a restore.

verifiedBy.note: fresh dir → initialized at app version; dir with stores and no marker → adopted at 1.2.0

requirements.title: Version-gated migration registry and runner
requirements.text: Migration steps { version, description, up() } shall be registered once per version in backend/src/services/migrationSteps/; the registry shall throw at load on a non-MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH or duplicate version and shall be sorted ascending. At boot and after a restore, runDataMigrations shall apply exactly the steps with dataVersion < step.version <= appVersion in order, advancing the marker after EACH step (action "migrated", with the step’s changed flag and details) and finally to the app version. A step that throws shall stop the start (exit 1) with the marker left at the previous step and a data-migration-failed audit entry; a completed run shall write a data-migrated audit entry. Steps shall be idempotent and re-runnable. A version bump with no due step shall only advance the marker.

verifiedBy.note: dataVersion 0.0.0 → every step runs once; a second boot changes nothing

requirements.title: The shape-normalizing pass is retained and runs first
requirements.text: The unconditional, idempotent shape-normalizing migrations (org-unit bootstrap, localized texts, materials, durations, question shape, training versions, ack pruning, SCORM thumbnails, SCORM GC) shall keep running on every boot and after every restore, BEFORE the version-gated steps and independent of the data version, so a legacy record planted into a current-version directory is still normalized.

verifiedBy.note: a durationHours record in a directory marked at the app version is converted at the next boot

requirements.title: Pre-migration backup
requirements.text: When at least one version-gated step is due, runDataMigrations shall create a backup with source "pre-migration" (archive name suffix -pre-migration) BEFORE the first step runs; the decision shall depend only on the version gap, never on the steps’ outcome. No backup shall be taken when no step is due, nor on the restore path (its pre-restore snapshot is the recovery point). Pre-migration archives shall be exempt from automatic-backup retention.

verifiedBy.note: exactly one pre-migration archive when a step is due; none on a fresh directory

requirements.title: Boot refusal on data from a newer version
requirements.text: When the marker’s dataVersion is greater than the app version, the backend shall log an error naming both versions and the way back and exit with code 1 before binding any listener, leaving the marker untouched. Setting ALLOW_DATA_DOWNGRADE=1 shall let it start with a loud warning instead; the marker shall never be moved downward.

verifiedBy.note: dataVersion 99.0.0 → exit 1 naming both versions; with ALLOW_DATA_DOWNGRADE=1 it boots

requirements.title: Version-aware backup archives and restore
requirements.text: Backup manifests shall be formatVersion 2, recording dataVersion and appVersion, and the archive shall carry data/_meta.json as a read-only passenger (never in the manifest’s files, never swapped). validateArchive shall derive the archive’s data version from the manifest, else the passenger, else the baseline 1.2.0, and shall never reject on version grounds (uploads stay permissive). restoreBackup shall refuse an archive whose data version exceeds the app version with HTTP 409 before the pre-restore snapshot or any write; otherwise, after swapping the stores, it shall write the marker to the archive’s version (action "restored") so the migrations run by the route bring the restored data up to date.

verifiedBy.note: v1 archive restores and is migrated; 99.0.0 archive → 409 with data unchanged

requirements.title: Release procedure
requirements.text: A release shall be cut with the /release skill: refuse on a dirty tree, a non-MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH target, a non-increasing version or an existing tag; decide whether a migration step is needed (removed/renamed persisted field, destructive prune or re-interpreted value → step; additive-with-default or shape-detectable → none) and scaffold it; write VERSION; run tools/sync-version.mjs; add a CHANGELOG.md section (Keep a Changelog) with a mandatory Data migrations subsection; run npm run verify; commit chore(release): X.Y.Z; create the annotated tag vX.Y.Z.

verifiedBy.note: CHANGELOG has a section for the current VERSION with Data migrations; the skill exists; sync-version --check passes

requirements.title: Migration 1.3.0: prune settings keys outside the Settings shape
requirements.text: The 1.3.0 step shall remove every top-level key of settings.json that is not a key of the default settings shape (in particular the removed materialLocales list, which the shallow merge in readSettings and the spread in PUT /api/settings otherwise preserve forever), leaving all known keys untouched, and shall report changed=false when nothing was pruned.
