With SMTP not configured, observe the hint to set it up.
Verify Settings exposes SMTP fields and the saved password is never returned (redacted).
tests.expected: The page sends via POST /api/mail/send; when SMTP is unconfigured the API returns 503 and the UI prompts to configure it in Settings; the SMTP password is redacted by the API.

tests.title: Back up all application data
tests.preconditions: Signed in as an administrator; at least one training with an uploaded material file exists.
steps: Create a backup and note the returned descriptor.
Download the archive and inspect its entries.
Confirm the six JSON stores, the material bytes and their sidecars, and a manifest are present.
Confirm no TLS key material and no nested backups are present.
tests.expected: A single ZIP is stored server-side and downloadable; it contains manifest.json plus data/users.json, roles, trainings, sessions, orgUnits, settings and every material file byte-for-byte; it contains no tls/ entry and no nested backups/.

tests.title: List backups and download one
tests.preconditions: Signed in as an administrator with at least one backup stored.
steps: Open the Backups page.
Read the row for a backup: archive name, creation date, size, contents and origin.
Use its Download action.
tests.expected: Every stored backup is listed newest first with name, date, size and contents; downloading yields the archive under its server-issued braingain-backup-*.zip name.

tests.title: Download all backups as one file
tests.preconditions: Signed in as an administrator with several backups stored.
steps: Open the Backups page.
Use the Download all action.
Inspect the downloaded file.
tests.expected: One braingain-backups-*.zip is downloaded containing every stored archive under its own name, and each entry is itself a valid backup archive.

tests.title: Upload a backup archive, with invalid files refused
tests.preconditions: Signed in as an administrator; a previously downloaded backup archive is available.
steps: Open the Backups page and upload the archive.
Upload a file that is not a backup (arbitrary bytes named .zip).
Also try a real ZIP without a BrainGain manifest, and one whose manifest lists a missing file.
tests.expected: The valid archive is stored and listed as uploaded, with its contents read from the archive; each invalid file is refused with a reason and adds nothing to the list.

tests.title: Restore replaces all data, is confirmed and undoable
tests.preconditions: Signed in as an administrator; a backup of a known state exists.
steps: Change data after the backup was taken (rename a training, add a job role).
Restore the backup — confirming the destructive action.
Re-read the changed data.
Restore the automatically created pre-restore snapshot.
Separately, attempt to restore a corrupt archive.
tests.expected: After the restore the post-backup changes are gone and the backed-up state is back; a pre-restore snapshot is listed and restoring it returns the newer state; the TLS certificate and the backup list survive; a corrupt archive is refused with the dataset untouched and no staging directory left behind.

tests.title: Backup functions are administrator-only
tests.preconditions: Tokens for an administrator, a trainer and a member; at least one backup stored.
steps: Call list, create, download, download-all, upload, restore and delete with no token.
Repeat each call as a trainer and as a member.
Confirm the Backups page and its sidebar link are not reachable for a non-admin.
Delete a backup as an administrator.
tests.expected: Every endpoint answers 401 without a token and 403 for a trainer or member, returning no archive bytes and changing nothing; a non-admin visiting /backups is redirected to the dashboard and sees no Backups link; an administrator can delete a backup, which removes the archive and its descriptor.

tests.title: A question with several correct answers
tests.preconditions: Signed in as a trainer.
steps: Create a training, add a question and four options.
Tick three of the four answers as correct.
Save, reload and reopen the training.
Try to untick the only remaining correct answer of a fresh question.
tests.expected: Several answers can be ticked correct and all of them come back after a reload; the last remaining correct answer cannot be unticked, so a question always keeps at least one.

tests.title: Exact-set grading of a multi-answer question
tests.preconditions: A training with a question having three of four options correct, assigned to the learner.
steps: Submit exactly the three correct options; repeat shuffled and with duplicates.
Submit a subset of them.
Submit every option.
On a single-answer question, submit the correct option plus one more, and submit nothing.
Inspect the learner payload for the question.
tests.expected: Only the exact set scores; order and duplicates are irrelevant; a subset scores 0 (no partial credit) and so does selecting everything; extra ticks on a single-answer question and an empty selection are wrong. The learner payload contains only id, text, options and type — neither the correct answers nor how many there are.

tests.title: Legacy single-answer questions keep working
tests.preconditions: A question supplied in the previous single-answer shape.
steps: Send a question carrying the legacy correctIndex field.
Read it back and inspect the persisted record.
tests.expected: The legacy scalar becomes a one-element answer key, grading against it behaves as before, and the legacy field is not persisted.

tests.title: Switching a question's type in the editor
tests.preconditions: Signed in as a trainer.
steps: Create a training with a saved multiple-choice question (one correct answer among three options).
Reopen it and switch the question to single choice.
Pick a different option as correct via the radio key, save and reload.
On a fresh question, mark two answers correct and try to switch to single choice; then untick one.
tests.expected: The switch to single choice is offered on the existing question and persists together with the moved answer key; while two answers are correct the single-choice switch is disabled, and reducing the key to one enables it again.

tests.title: A learner answers a single-choice question with radio buttons
tests.preconditions: A training with one single-choice question assigned to the learner.
steps: Open the training session and start the test.
Observe the controls for the single-choice question.
Select one option, then select another.
Submit with the correct option selected.
tests.expected: The question is rendered as radio buttons and no checkboxes — the control type alone carries the single-choice semantics, with no textual prompt; picking a second option replaces the first instead of adding to it; the submission grades and passes.

tests.title: Question type persistence, coercion and grading
tests.preconditions: Trainer, admin and learner accounts.
steps: Create questions with type 'single', with no type, and with type 'single' but several correct answers; read them back and after an update.
Fetch the training as the learner and inspect a question's fields.
Grade a single-choice question with the correct answer, with the correct answer plus an extra one, and with an empty selection.
tests.expected: The type round-trips and an untyped question is persisted as multiple-choice; 'single' with several correct answers is coerced to multiple-choice with the key intact; the learner payload is exactly { id, text, options, type } with no answer key; only the exact one-element selection scores — an API-forged multi-selection and an empty selection are wrong.

tests.title: Reveal-wrong-questions option: default, toggle and grade response
tests.preconditions: Admin, trainer and learner accounts; trainings with known answer keys.
steps: Read the settings and fail an attempt with the option at its default.
Enable the option as admin and fail an attempt answering one of three questions right.
Pass an attempt at exactly the threshold with one question wrong.
Disable the option again and fail another attempt.
tests.expected: The option defaults to off and no wrong-question list appears; enabled, the failed response names exactly the wrongly answered questions by index and nothing else (no answer key); the passed-but-imperfect attempt carries no list; after disabling, the list disappears again.

tests.title: A failing learner sees which questions were wrong
tests.preconditions: Admin account; a two-question training assigned to the learner; the option enabled.
steps: As admin, open Settings and locate the reveal toggle.
As the learner, fail the test by answering the first question wrong and the second right.
Inspect the failed result screen.
tests.expected: The Settings pass-threshold card offers the toggle (off by default); the failed result lists the wrongly answered question by its text and not the correctly answered one.

tests.title: Per-language material variants round-trip and sanitize
tests.preconditions: Trainer account; default material languages (en, de).
steps: Create a training with a material carrying a German and an English variant, each with its own label and link; read it back and update it.
Send variants with unknown locales, without content, with duplicate locales, and with both a url and an uploaded file.
Send a material whose variants all fail sanitization.
tests.expected: Variants round-trip with their own labels and content, ordered by the settings list; unknown-locale and content-less variants are dropped, the first variant per locale wins, an uploaded file wins over a url, and a material with no surviving variant is dropped entirely — at least one variant per stored material.

tests.title: Legacy material is migrated to English variants
tests.preconditions: A data directory whose trainings carry the pre-locale materialLinks/materialFiles shape.
steps: Boot the backend against the legacy data.
Read the trainings via the API and inspect the store on disk.
tests.expected: Every legacy link and file is now the single English variant of its own material (files named after the file), fully empty legacy rows are dropped, and the legacy fields are gone from the API payload and from disk.

tests.title: Authoring and consuming localized material
tests.preconditions: Trainer and learner accounts; content languages are English and German.
steps: As a trainer, fill the English and German rows of one material with their own labels and links, save and reopen.
As a learner whose language is German, open a session over a DE+EN material and an EN-only material.
tests.expected: The editor round-trips both variants and its summary reports the material count and languages; the learner sees the German variant unadorned and the English variant standing in where German is missing, marked with its language flag.

tests.title: Profile language endpoint
tests.preconditions: Member and admin accounts.
steps: PUT the member's locale and read /me and a fresh login payload.
Send a non-UI locale and no token.
Start an impersonation session and attempt the PUT with its token.
tests.expected: The locale persists and every identity payload carries it; locales outside en/de are rejected (400) and anonymous writes 401; during impersonation the write is refused (403) and the target's profile stays untouched.

tests.title: Language switch persists across sign-ins
tests.preconditions: Member account with an English profile.
steps: Open the user menu and pick Deutsch on the flagged switch.
Sign out, clear the browser's remembered language, and sign in again.
tests.expected: The UI switches to German immediately, and the fresh sign-in comes up in German — the choice followed the profile, not the browser.

tests.title: Localized questions: round-trip, sanitization and migration
tests.preconditions: Trainer account; default material languages (en, de).
steps: Create a question with German and English text and answers; read it back.
Send an unconfigured language, an option empty in every language, and a question with no text at all.
Grade an attempt by option index.
Boot the backend against a data set whose questions are plain strings.
tests.expected: Both languages round-trip with the answer key untouched; the unconfigured language and the empty option are dropped (key remapped), the textless question vanishes; grading is index-based and language-independent; legacy plain strings come up as English entries after boot.

tests.title: Authoring and taking a quiz in the learner's language
tests.preconditions: Trainer and learner accounts; the learner's profile language is German.
steps: As a trainer, fill a question's text and answers in the English and German rows, save and reopen.
As the learner, take a quiz with one DE+EN question and one English-only question.
Answer correctly and submit.
As an English-language learner, open a quiz with a German-only question.
tests.expected: Both languages round-trip into their rows in the editor; the learner sees the German question and answers, the English-only question stands in wearing the English flag, and the attempt passes — grading ignores the display language; the German-only question shows the English learner the German text wearing the German flag.

tests.title: Dashboard due-only filter
tests.preconditions: A learner with at least one due training and one passed (up-to-date) training.
steps: Open the dashboard and inspect the filter checkbox.
Look for the up-to-date training.
Uncheck the filter.
Reload the dashboard and inspect the filter again.
tests.expected: The "only show due trainings" filter is checked by default and the up-to-date training is hidden while due trainings show; unchecking reveals it with its up-to-date status; after a reload the filter is still unchecked — the choice is persisted to the profile.

tests.title: Localized training master data: round-trip, sanitization and migration
tests.preconditions: Trainer account; default material languages (en, de).
steps: Create a training with German and English name, description and category; read it back.
Send an unconfigured language, blank language entries, and creates without a usable name.
Create and update trainings with legacy plain-string fields; omit fields on update.
Boot the backend against a data set whose name/description/category are plain strings.
tests.expected: Both languages round-trip; unconfigured and blank languages are dropped; a create whose name has no language is refused (400) while description/category may end up empty; legacy strings coerce to English entries on write, omitted fields keep their stored values, and plain-string records come up as English entries (an empty string as an empty map) after boot.

tests.title: Authoring a bilingual training name and seeing it in the learner's language
tests.preconditions: Trainer and learner accounts; the learner's profile language is German.
steps: As a trainer, fill the training name's English and German rows in the Basics section, save and reopen.
Require the training from the learner and set the learner's profile language to German.
Open the learner's dashboard.
tests.expected: Both name values round-trip into their own language rows in the editor; the learner's dashboard card shows the German name and the English one appears nowhere.

tests.title: Automatic scheduled backups — interval, catch-up and retention
tests.preconditions: Administrator account; a data directory the test can restart the server against.
steps: Read the settings and confirm automatic backups default to disabled with a 7-day interval and a keep-count of 5; save out-of-range and junk values and read back what was stored.
Enable automation in the stored settings, plant a backdated automatic backup, restart the server and wait for the boot catch-up; also restart once with a fresh-enough automatic backup.
With keep = 2, plant three backdated automatic backups plus one manual backup, restart, and let a due run complete.
Disable automation, plant a long-overdue automatic backup, restart and wait.
tests.expected: Defaults are off / 7 days / keep 5, and saved values are clamped to 1..365 days and 1..100 kept (junk falls back to the defaults). An overdue — or missing — newest automatic backup triggers exactly one fresh backup with source 'auto' at boot, while a fresh-enough one triggers none. After the due run only the newest two automatic backups remain, deleted archives are gone from disk, and the manual backup survives untouched. With automation disabled no automatic backup is created however overdue.

tests.title: Configuring automatic backups from the Settings page
tests.preconditions: Signed in as an administrator.
steps: Open Settings and locate the Automatic backups card.
Confirm the defaults: disabled, back up every 7 days, keep 5 automatic backups.
Enable the schedule, set the interval to 3 days and the keep-count to 2, and save.
Reload the page.
tests.expected: The card shows the shipped defaults (off / 7 / 5); saving reports success; after the reload the card comes back enabled with interval 3 and keep 2.

tests.title: Audit entries for mutations, authentication events and completions — content and redaction
tests.preconditions: Administrator account; a data directory the test can read audit.ndjson from.
steps: Create, update and delete a user (the update changing the name, password and assigned roles) and read the audit log.
Save settings with a changed SMTP password and edit a training’s questions; read the log again.
Sign in successfully and with a wrong password, activate an imported account, and impersonate a user.
Pass one grading run and fail another.
Append a broken half-line to the log file and list the entries again.
tests.expected: Every mutation, authentication event and the passed completion each appear as one entry with timestamp, actor and entity; updates carry field diffs with each assigned role shown as its name followed by its id; password, SMTP password and question changes are masked as ***; the failed sign-in entry has no actor and only the attempted email; the failed grading attempt writes no entry; the torn line is skipped without losing the rest.

tests.title: Audit log travels in backups and survives restore
tests.preconditions: Administrator account with some audit history.
steps: Create a backup and open the archive.
Perform further audited actions, then restore the backup.
List the audit entries after the restore.
tests.expected: The archive contains data/audit.ndjson but the manifest's files list does not name it; after the restore every entry written before the restore is still present, followed by a backup-restore entry naming the safety backup — the archived copy was not imported.

tests.title: Audit read API — access control, filters, paging and CSV export
tests.preconditions: Administrator and non-administrator accounts; several audit entries of different actions.
steps: Call GET /api/audit without a token and as a non-administrator.
As an administrator, list entries filtered by action, entity type, free text and a date range, paged with offset/limit.
Download /api/audit/export.csv with a filter applied.
tests.expected: Unauthenticated and non-admin calls are rejected (401/403); the filtered list returns { total, entries } newest first and paging slices it consistently; the CSV arrives as an attachment with a header row, one row per filtered entry, RFC-4180 quoting and formula-injection guarding.

tests.title: Inspecting, filtering and exporting the audit trail in the app
tests.preconditions: Signed in as an administrator; at least one auditable action performed.
steps: Perform an audited change (e.g. edit a job role), open the Audit trail page from the sidebar.
Filter by the action and expand the entry’s changes.
Click Export CSV.
Sign in as a non-administrator and look for the page.
tests.expected: The new entry is listed with actor and action; the expanded row shows the changed fields with before/after values; the export downloads a CSV file; a non-administrator has no Audit trail navigation entry and /audit redirects to the dashboard.

tests.title: Materials confirmation is audited and a test-less training completes by confirmation
tests.preconditions: A learner account; a training without test questions.
steps: As the learner, call POST /api/sessions/confirm-materials for the training and read the audit trail.
Call it with an unknown trainingId and without a token.
Grade the question-less training with an empty answer set and read the sessions and the audit trail.
tests.expected: The confirmation appends one 'materials-confirmed' entry with the learner as actor, the training as entity and the material count in the details; the unknown-id call is a 404 and the anonymous call a 401, neither writing an entry; the empty grading passes at 100%, persists a session, and appends the training-completed entry.

tests.title: The confirmation dialog gates the test and completes a test-less training in the app
tests.preconditions: A learner with an assigned training that has material; one variant of the training without questions.
steps: Open the training session and click the start action.
Cancel the confirmation dialog, then start again and confirm.
Repeat for a training without questions.
As an administrator, open the audit trail.
tests.expected: The dialog states the learner confirms awareness of all provided materials; cancelling stays on the material step and starts no test; confirming starts the quiz. For the training without questions the start action is enabled, and confirming completes the training with a confirmation-based success message. The audit trail lists the materials-confirmed entries.

tests.title: Trainer contact endpoint returns name, org unit and email
tests.preconditions: A training owned by a trainer who belongs to an organizational unit.
steps: Call GET /api/trainings/:id/trainer as a member and compare the fields against the owner's user record and unit.
Call it without a token and with an unknown training id.
tests.expected: The response carries exactly the owner's name, email and organizational-unit name (no other user fields, in particular no secrets); the anonymous call is a 401 and the unknown id a 404.

tests.title: The trainer contact hint appears in the confirmation dialog and on the result screen
tests.preconditions: Signed in as a learner with an assigned training.
steps: Open the training session and click the start action.
Read the confirmation dialog's trainer hint.
Confirm, answer the test wrongly and submit.
tests.expected: The dialog and the failed result screen both show the hint naming the trainer, their organizational unit and their email address (as a mailto link), so the trainee can find the trainer in the address list.

tests.title: Editing a training without being overwhelmed
tests.preconditions: Trainer/admin participants; a training that already has three questions, a link and a file.
steps: Task: "Change the duration of this training."
Task: "Add a fourth question to it."
Task: "Tell me, without opening anything, how many questions this training has."
Observe scrolling, wrong turns, and whether participants use the section headers.
tests.expected: Participants reach the field they need without scrolling through unrelated parts, add a question and type into it straight away, and read the question count off the collapsed section header.
tests.metric: Task success ≥ 90%; no participant scrolls past more than one screen to reach a field; the question count is read off the header by ≥ 4/5.

tests.title: Publish a training update: explicit step, authorization and validation
tests.preconditions: Seeded backend; trainer owns a training a member has passed; SMTP unconfigured.
steps: Attempt publish-update anonymously, as a member and as a non-owner trainer.
Attempt publishes with a bad mode, a past deadline and empty email fields.
Publish a valid confirm-mode update as the owner; save the training via the editor UI with and without a content change.
tests.expected: Anonymous 401, member and non-owner trainer 403; invalid payloads 400 with nothing recorded; a valid publish returns 201 with the update, bumped version and affected/email report; in the UI only a content-changing save offers the publish dialog, skipping keeps the change as an unpublished draft, and the save itself never notifies.

tests.title: The 'updated' due state: audience and earliest-deadline selection
tests.preconditions: A member passed the training before the update was published; a second training was never taken.
steps: Publish an update and read /trainings/mine, /trainings/trainees and the dashboard.
Publish a second update with an earlier deadline and acknowledge it.
tests.expected: The prior completer flips to 'updated' with dueDate = the update deadline and the pending update payload; a never-taker stays 'never'; the dashboard shows the distinct badge and includes it in the due filter; with several pending updates the earliest deadline governs, and acknowledging a newer confirm update never clears an older retake update.

tests.title: Confirm-mode acknowledgement: persisted, idempotent, audited, quiz-free
tests.preconditions: A confirm-mode update is pending for the signed-in learner ('updated' state).
steps: Open the session, review the update banner and confirm the updated materials.
Repeat the confirmation; attempt to acknowledge a retake-mode update.
Delete the training and inspect the acknowledgement store.
tests.expected: The confirmation is persisted and audited ('training-update-confirmed'), clears the 'updated' state without a quiz and without touching the cycle date; a repeat is idempotent; acknowledging a retake-mode update is rejected (400); deleting a training removes its acknowledgements.

tests.title: Cycle precedence and cycle reset on retake
tests.preconditions: A retake-mode update is pending; the pass history can be backdated in the test data dir.
steps: Pass the training again while the retake update is pending.
Backdate the last pass beyond the cycle grace window with updates still published.
tests.expected: A new passing session clears the retake update and restarts the regular cycle (dueDate = new pass + cycleYears); with the cycle overdue the status reports 'overdue', not 'updated' — the cycle takes precedence and no pending update is surfaced.

tests.title: Publishing tolerates email failure
tests.preconditions: SMTP unconfigured at first, then configured against an unreachable server.
steps: Publish with SMTP unconfigured.
Configure SMTP against an unreachable host and publish again.
Publish on a training nobody has passed.
tests.expected: Every publish succeeds (201) and records the update; the email report says skipped:'not-configured', failed:true, and skipped:'no-recipients' respectively — email problems never block the update.

tests.title: Withdraw a published update
tests.preconditions: A published update exists, one learner has acknowledged it.
steps: Withdraw the update as a member, as the owner, and with an unknown update id.
Inspect the training, the acknowledgement store and the audit trail.
tests.expected: Member → 403; owner → 204: the update disappears, its acknowledgements are pruned, the withdrawal is audited ('training-update-cancelled' naming the version) and the training version stays; unknown update → 404.

tests.title: Training version lifecycle
tests.preconditions: Seeded backend; a legacy training record without a version can be injected into the data dir.
steps: Create a training and read its version; attempt to alter version/updates via PUT.
Publish updates and observe the version and the version stamped on each update.
Publish on a legacy record without a version field; view a card on the dashboard.
tests.expected: A new training starts at version 0 (unpublished) with no updates and empty published content; PUT cannot inject updates, a draft object or alter the version (server-managed); each publish increments the version and stamps it on notify-update records; a legacy record without a version publishes as version 2 (implicit 1); the dashboard card shows no version number (learner-facing views carry none).

tests.title: Draft staging & published-only visibility
tests.preconditions: Seeded backend; a training published as v1 with a differing draft staged on top.
steps: Create a training with content and inspect the response; PUT metadata and content changes.
Read the training as a learner (/:id, the list, /mine) and as the owner.
Inspect the audit diff of a content-staging PUT; reboot the server with a version-0 record on disk.
tests.expected: Creation yields version 0 with the content staged in a timestamped draft; PUT applies metadata live, stages content, clears the draft on equality and preserves savedAt for unchanged content; learners receive the published content only and never a draft field, while the owner sees the WIP; the audit records the change as a masked 'draft' field (no answer key on disk); a reboot never promotes version 0.

tests.title: Silent publish
tests.preconditions: A version-0 training with a draft; a published training without a draft.
steps: Publish the draft with kind silent; read the training back.
Attempt kind silent without a draft, kind notify at version 0, an unknown kind, and a kind-less notify publish.
Stage a draft on a passed training and publish with kind notify.
tests.expected: The silent publish promotes the draft (0→1), clears it, appends no update, sends no email and responds with only the version; silent-without-draft, notify-at-v0 and unknown kinds are 400; omitting kind behaves as notify; a notify publish with a draft promotes the content AND creates the obligation for prior completers.

tests.title: Unpublished trainings cannot be completed
tests.preconditions: A version-0 training assigned to the learner.
steps: Grade the unpublished training via the API (empty answers).
Open the learner dashboard and the training session by deep link.
tests.expected: Grading is refused with 409 and no session is persisted (the zero-questions auto-pass cannot fire); the dashboard card shows a neutral "In preparation" state with a disabled Start and no version number; the session page shows the in-preparation notice instead of the material/quiz flow.

tests.title: Discard a draft
tests.preconditions: A published training with a staged draft, including a draft-only uploaded file.
steps: Attempt the discard anonymously, as a member and as a non-owner trainer.
Discard as the owner (UI: the versions dialog); repeat the discard; inspect the file bytes.
tests.expected: Anonymous 401, member and non-owner trainer 403; the owner's discard reverts the editor content to the published state, is audited ('training-draft-discarded') and 404s when nothing is left to discard; draft-only file bytes are deleted while published bytes and the version stay; replacing a draft file deletes the replaced draft upload, and a publish deletes the superseded published upload.

tests.title: Completion signature verification rules
tests.preconditions: Seeded backend against the stub IdP; published trainings with and without questions; an SSO-provisioned account.
steps: Grade without credentials, with a wrong password and with the correct password.
Impersonate the member as an admin and grade with each of their passwords.
Sign with a fresh Microsoft token for the linked account, a stale one, and one for a different account.
tests.expected: Missing/wrong credentials → 403, nothing persisted, a 'login-failed' audit entry naming the acting account and reason; the correct password (or a fresh, oid-matching Microsoft token) completes the training and the 'training-completed' audit entry carries 'signed: password|microsoft'; the impersonator's own credentials never sign — only the acting account's do; stale or foreign Microsoft tokens are refused.

tests.title: Completion signature in the session UI
tests.preconditions: Signed in as a learner with an assigned, published training.
steps: Complete a test-less training: enter a wrong password in the confirmation dialog, then the correct one.
Submit a quiz: the signature dialog gates the submission.
Open the audit trail as an administrator and filter for completions.
tests.expected: The wrong password shows the failure message and keeps the learner in the dialog to retry; the correct password completes the training; every quiz submission opens the identity dialog first; the audit page shows the completion with its signature method.

tests.title: Reordered content persists and grades correctly
tests.preconditions: A published training with two materials and two questions.
steps: PUT the training with materials and questions reversed and one question’s options reversed with a remapped key.
Publish the draft and read the training as a learner; grade with the new option indices.
tests.expected: The new order is staged as the draft (the published order untouched until publish); after publishing, materials, questions and options arrive in the arranged order and the remapped key grades the same answers correctly.

tests.title: Reorder buttons in the editor
tests.preconditions: Signed in as the owning trainer; a training with several materials, questions and options.
steps: Move a material down, a question up and the correct answer option up using the row buttons.
Save (keeping the change as a draft), reopen the editor.
tests.expected: Each move swaps the rows immediately, the boundary buttons are disabled, the answer-key marker follows the moved option, and the new order (including the key) survives save and reopen.

tests.title: The trainings list shows the version and the date of the last update
tests.preconditions: Signed in as a trainer; the seeded (published) trainings plus a freshly created one.
steps: Create a training without publishing it and read its list row.
Read the list row of a published training.
tests.expected: The unpublished training’s row shows no version and is flagged "Not published yet"; the published training’s version line shows "Version 1 · <date of the last update>". API-side, every publish (silent included) stamps publishedAt on the training, and a never-published training carries none.

tests.title: The build produces CycloneDX SBOMs for backend and frontend
tests.preconditions: Repository checked out with dependencies installed (npm install in backend and frontend).
steps: Run `npm run sbom` at the repository root (the same generation runs as the last step of each package build).
Open sbom/backend.cdx.json and sbom/frontend.cdx.json and inspect the content.
tests.expected: Both files are valid CycloneDX JSON (bomFormat "CycloneDX", specVersion 1.x) whose metadata.component names braingain-backend / braingain-frontend; the component list contains the runtime dependencies (e.g. express and jsonwebtoken, vue and pinia) with package URLs, and no dev-only tooling (typescript, tsx, vite).

tests.title: SCORM 1.2 package import

Grade under the exit and time rules.

tests.title: Data from a newer version is refused

tests.title: Restore is version-aware

tests.title: Concurrent users never lose a record
tests.preconditions: A freshly seeded backend; an admin session.

Have eight learners pass the same training with simultaneous grade requests; read each learner's sessions.

The double grade yields one 200 and one 409 with exactly one session and one audit entry for the attempt; the double launch returns the same attempt id. No .tmp file lingers and every store parses. The corrupt-store request answers a JSON 500 while /api/health stays 200.
